title: 584. Mary, Queen of Scots: Birth of a Legend (Part 1)

sentences.en: She held the crucifix high, visible all down the long hall, as she flung defiance at her judges,
sentences.zh: 她高高举起十字架，在长厅的各处都能看到，同时她向法官们公然宣示反抗，

sentences.en: and her voice rose with a kind of triumph above the voice of the Dean of Peterborough, always higher and clearer than his rising tones, arching over the vehement English prayers,
sentences.zh: 她的声音带着一种胜利般的激昂，压过了彼得伯勒教务长那始终更高更清晰的声音，在激烈、富有感染力的英语祈祷声中回荡，

sentences.en: the mysterious dominating invocations of the ancient faith.
sentences.zh: 那是古老信仰中神秘而主导的祈祷词。

sentences.en: The Queen's voice held on for a minute after the clergyman had finished.
sentences.zh: 在牧师结束诵读后，女王的声音又持续了一分钟。

sentences.en: Her words were in English now.
sentences.zh: 她现在用英语说。

sentences.en: She was praying for the people of England, and for the soul of her royal cousin Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 她在为英格兰人民祈祷，也为她高贵的表姐伊丽莎白的灵魂祈祷。

sentences.en: She was forgiving all her enemies.
sentences.zh: 她在宽恕所有的敌人。

sentences.en: Then, for a moment, her ladies were busy about her.
sentences.zh: 然后，有一会儿，她的女官们围着她忙碌起来。

sentences.en: The black velvet gown fell below her knees, revealing underbodice and petticoat of crimson silk, and she stepped forward suddenly, shockingly, in the colour of martyrdom,
sentences.zh: 黑色的丝绒长裙落到膝盖以下，露出了里面深红色的内衣和衬裙，她突然跨步向前，带着令人震惊的殉道者的色彩，

sentences.en: blood red from top to toe against the sombre background.
sentences.zh: 在一片阴暗的背景衬托下，从头到脚血红一片。

sentences.en: Quietly she knelt and bowed herself low over the little chopping block.
sentences.zh: 她平静地跪下，深深地鞠躬贴在那个小断头台面上。

sentences.en: In manus tuas domine, and they heard twice the dull chunk of the axe.
sentences.zh: 主啊，我将灵魂交托于你，人们听到两声沉闷的斧头砍击声。

sentences.en: There was one more ceremony to accomplish.
sentences.zh: 还有一个仪式需要完成。

sentences.en: The executioner must exhibit the head and speak the customary words.
sentences.zh: 刽子手必须展示人头并说出习俗惯例的话语。

sentences.en: The masked black figure stooped and rose, crying in a loud voice,
sentences.zh: 那个戴着面具的黑色身影弯腰又直起，大声喊道，

sentences.en: Long live the Queen!
sentences.zh: 女王万岁！

sentences.en: But all he held in his hand that had belonged to the rival Queen of Hearts was a kerchief, and pinned to it an elaborate auburn wig.
sentences.zh: 但他手里拿着的、曾属于那位红心女王情敌的东西，只是一块手帕，上面还别着一顶精致的红棕色假发。

sentences.en: Rolled nearer the edge of the platform, shrunken and withered and grey, with a sparse silver stubble on the small, shiny skull, was the head of the martyr.
sentences.zh: 滚到讲台边缘的是那位殉道者的头颅，它已经萎缩、枯槁、发灰，那个小巧发光的头骨上稀稀拉拉地长着几根银色的胡茬。

sentences.en: Mary Stewart had always known how to embarrass her enemies.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·斯图尔特总是知道如何让她的敌人们感到尴尬。

sentences.en: So that was the American historian Garrett Mattingly in 1950, and he was writing about the execution of Mary Stewart.
sentences.zh: 那是1950年的美国历史学家加勒特·马廷利，他当时正在撰写关于玛丽·斯图尔特处决的文章。

sentences.en: Mary, Queen of Scots, of Fotheringay Castle on the 8th of February, 1587.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰女王玛丽，于1587年2月8日在弗瑟林海城堡（被处决）。

sentences.en: Tom Holland, it is one of the most dramatic, one of the most celebrated moments in British history.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰德，这是英国历史上最戏剧性、最著名的时刻之一。

sentences.en: Iconic, because Mary is a bit of an icon, isn't she?
sentences.zh: 具有标志性，因为玛丽本身就是一个偶像，对吧？

sentences.en: She's a fashion icon.
sentences.zh: 她是个时尚偶像。

sentences.en: She is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: She's famously beautiful and stylish and well-dressed and all of these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 她以美貌、时尚、会穿搭以及诸如此类的事情而闻名。

sentences.en: And also loads of history about men.
sentences.zh: 而且这里面还牵涉到大量关于男人的历史。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But now we're absolutely hitting the jackpot.
sentences.zh: 但现在我们绝对是大赚特赚了。

sentences.en: So I would say Mary, Queen of Scots is probably the most celebrated Scot who's ever lived, and she's celebrated because she is a byword for glamour and romance and tragedy,
sentences.zh: 所以我想说，苏格兰女王玛丽可能是苏格兰有史以来最著名的人，她之所以闻名，是因为她是迷人、浪漫和悲剧的代名词，

sentences.en: which seems to be what people like in Scottish history.
sentences.zh: 而这似乎正是人们在苏格兰历史中所喜爱的。

sentences.en: So I guess Bonnie Prince Charlie would perhaps be her only rival, who's also glamorous, romantic and tragic.
sentences.zh: 所以我想邦妮·王子查理或许是她唯一的竞争对手，他也同样迷人、浪漫而悲惨。

sentences.en: The story of Mary, Queen of Scots is extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰女王玛丽的故事非同寻常。

sentences.en: So she becomes the Queen of Scots when she's only one week old.
sentences.zh: 她在年仅一岁（原文为one week old，译者意译为一周大，这里遵从原文译为出生仅一周）时就成了苏格兰女王。

sentences.en: She then goes to France, and as a teenager, she briefly rules as Queen of France.
sentences.zh: 后来她去了法国，并在十几岁时短暂地统治过法兰西，成为法国王后。

sentences.en: And then when she's 19, she comes back to Scotland, a country that she barely remembers.
sentences.zh: 当她19岁时，她回到了苏格兰，一个她几乎毫无记忆的国家。

sentences.en: And she has this incredibly convulsive and ultimately calamitous reign, which is marked by plots and rebellions and two disastrous marriages and two very notorious murders.
sentences.zh: 她经历了这场极其动荡、最终充满灾难的统治，其标志是阴谋、叛乱、两场灾难性的婚姻以及两起臭昭昭的谋杀案。

sentences.en: And as a result, mystery and controversy completely shadows her.
sentences.zh: 因此，神秘和争议彻底笼罩了她。

sentences.en: So there are all kinds of questions that people are always debating.
sentences.zh: 所以人们总是在争论各种各样的问题。

sentences.en: Was she an adulteress?
sentences.zh: 她是个通奸者吗？

sentences.en: Was she a murderess?
sentences.zh: 她是个谋杀犯吗？

sentences.en: Was she a victim of rape?
sentences.zh: 她是强奸的受害者吗？

sentences.en: And she's a very polarizing figure, and she always has been.
sentences.zh: 她是一个非常两极分化的温和人物，而且一直都是如此。

sentences.en: So to her admirers, of whom there are lots, she's the archetype of a heroine brought low by duplicitous and brutal men.
sentences.zh: 因此，在她的崇拜者（为数众多）眼中，她是那些被两面三刀且残忍的男性陷害的女英雄的典范。

sentences.en: So she was a figure of romance and now a kind of feminist heroine.
sentences.zh: 所以她曾是一个浪漫的人物，现在则成了一种女权主义女英雄。

sentences.en: But there are lots of people who think she's a complete waste of space, useless, a traitor, conniving, and an inept at conniving.
sentences.zh: 但也有很多人认为她完全是一无是处、毫无用处、是个叛徒、诡计多端，而且在搞阴谋诡计方面极其无能。

sentences.en: So that's even worse than conniving, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这甚至比诡计多端还要糟糕，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, she ends up deposed.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，她最后被废黜了。

sentences.en: You know, that's pretty much the marker of being a failure as a ruler.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这基本上就是作为一个统治者失败的标志。

sentences.en: And back in the 16th century, the justification for this was precisely that she was a Jezebel,
sentences.zh: 早在16世纪，这样做的正当理由正是因为她是一个耶洗别（淫妇），

sentences.en: that she was a kind of monstrous archetype of everything that made women rulers a terrible idea.
sentences.zh: 她是一种可怕的原型，代表了让女性成为统治者是个糟糕主意的一切。

sentences.en: And today, there are absolutely historians who will say that she's one of the most calamitous rulers in Scottish history.
sentences.zh: 而在今天，绝对有历史学家会说她是苏格兰历史上最具灾难性的统治者之一。

sentences.en: And the doyen of these historians who condemn her as a disastrous queen, who is herself Scottish, Jenny Wormald, wrote a brilliant, groundbreaking book on Mary, Queen of Scots.
sentences.zh: 谴责她是灾难女王的这些历史学家中的泰斗、本身就是苏格兰人的珍妮·沃马尔德，曾写过一本关于苏格兰女王玛丽的精彩、具有开创性的书。

sentences.en: And she condemned her as a monarch of little wit and no judgment, a woman who absolutely brought about her own downfall.
sentences.zh: 她谴责她是一个毫无智慧、全无判断力的君主，是一个亲手导致自己覆灭的女性。

sentences.en: And so, Dominic, we will be sifting the evidence for this today and over the next five episodes of the series.
sentences.zh: 因此，多米尼克，今天以及本系列的接下来五集里，我们将仔细甄别支持这一论点的证据。

sentences.en: And lots to discuss.
sentences.zh: 有太多内容要讨论了。

sentences.en: But important to emphasise, you were worried that this was maybe an overly Scottish theme.
sentences.zh: 但必须要强调的是，你曾担心这可能是一个过于苏格兰化的话题。

sentences.en: I wouldn't say worried.
sentences.zh: 我不会说担心。

sentences.en: I would say excited.
sentences.zh: 我应该说兴奋。

sentences.en: You would be relieved to know that this isn't just a Scottish story.
sentences.zh: 你可能会感到欣慰，因为这不仅仅是一个苏格兰的故事。

sentences.en: There's quite a lot of England in it as well.
sentences.zh: 里面也有相当多的英格兰元素。

sentences.en: And I guess that that's evident from the account of the execution that you read, which we opened this episode with.
sentences.zh: 我想，从你所宣读的处决记录中就可以明显看出这一点，我们就是以它来开启本集节目的。

sentences.en: Because Fotheringay, of course, where she ends up being beheaded, is in England.
sentences.zh: 因为弗瑟林海，也就是她最终被斩首的地方，当然是在英格兰。

sentences.en: I mean, it's in Middle England.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它在英格兰中部。

sentences.en: It's in Northamptonshire.
sentences.zh: 它在北安普敦郡。

sentences.en: But what that passage also alluded to is the sense in which, in death as throughout her adult life,
sentences.zh: 但那段文字也暗示了一种感觉，即在临死之时以及整个成年生活中，

sentences.en: Mary, Queen of Scots, is shadowed by a rival queen.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰女王玛丽始终被一个王位竞争对手的阴影所笼罩。

sentences.en: And this queen is her own cousin.
sentences.zh: 而这位女王就是她的表姐。

sentences.en: In fact, it's the woman who had agreed to her death.
sentences.zh: 事实上，正是那个同意判处她死刑的女人。

sentences.en: And that, of course, is Elizabeth Tudor.
sentences.zh: 当然，那就是伊丽莎白·都铎。

sentences.en: Elizabeth I.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白一世。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Mary was the Queen of Scots, Tom.
sentences.zh: 所以玛丽是苏格兰女王，汤姆。

sentences.en: Elizabeth was the Queen of England.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白是英格兰女王。

sentences.en: Mary was a Catholic.
sentences.zh: 玛丽是个天主教徒。

sentences.en: Elizabeth was a Protestant.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白是个新教徒。

sentences.en: And Mary, of course, was married three times.
sentences.zh: 当然，玛丽结过三次婚。

sentences.en: But Elizabeth was the Virgin Queen, married to her people and to her country.
sentences.zh: 但伊丽莎白是童贞女王，她将自己嫁给了她的臣民和她的国家。

sentences.en: And here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 问题就在这里。

sentences.en: We always think of them as the sort of supreme arch rivals.
sentences.zh: 我们总是把他们看作那种终极的死敌。

sentences.en: But they never actually met.
sentences.zh: 但他们实际上从未谋面。

sentences.en: They never even were in the same building at the same time.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至从未在同一时间出现在同一栋建筑里。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think that people ever since have felt that this was a slightly wasted opportunity.
sentences.zh: 我认为从那以后人们一直觉得这是一个有点可惜的机会。

sentences.en: And in so many fictional treatments of Mary, Queen of Scots, she's always meeting up with Elizabeth I.
sentences.zh: 在许多关于苏格兰女王玛丽的虚构作品中，她总是和伊丽莎白一世会面。

sentences.en: So Schiller in Germany wrote a famous play about it.
sentences.zh: 因此，德国的席勒写过一部关于此事的著名戏剧。

sentences.en: Donizetti wrote an opera, again, where Mary and Elizabeth meet up.
sentences.zh: 多尼采蒂写过一部歌剧，同样也是玛丽和伊丽莎白相遇。

sentences.en: And I suppose the most recent example is the 2018 film starring Saoirse Ronan as Mary, Queen of Scots.
sentences.zh: 我想最近的一个例子是2018年的电影，由西尔莎·罗南饰演苏格兰女王玛丽。

sentences.en: And actually, I have next to me, and I will hold it up for the benefit of those on YouTube, it's this titanic, definitive biography of Mary by John Guy,
sentences.zh: 实际上，我身边就有一本，为了YouTube观众的面子我会把它举起来，这是由约翰·盖伊撰写的关于玛丽的这本宏大、权威的传记，

sentences.en: which came out about 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 它大约在20年前出版。

sentences.en: And it's been retitled for the purposes of the film.
sentences.zh: 为了电影的需要，它被重新命名了。

sentences.en: And on the cover, you get Saoirse Ronan as Mary, Queen of Scots, but you also get Margot Robbie as Elizabeth I.
sentences.zh: 在封面上，你可以看到饰演苏格兰女王玛丽的西尔莎·罗南，但你也能看到饰演伊丽莎白一世的玛格特·罗比。

sentences.en: And the subtitle is Two Queens, One Future.
sentences.zh: 副标题是《双女王，一个未来》。

sentences.en: So that sense that to write about Mary immediately means that you have to write about Elizabeth is really, really powerful and part of the story that we'll be telling.
sentences.zh: 所以这种感觉——即要写玛丽就意味着你必须写伊丽莎白——真的是非常非常强烈，也是我们要讲述的故事的一部分。

sentences.en: But it's not just an English or Scottish story.
sentences.zh: 但这不仅仅是一个英格兰或苏格兰的故事。

sentences.en: It's also a European story, right?
sentences.zh: 这也是一个欧洲的故事，对吧？

sentences.en: Because as you've pointed out, the book that we read from in the beginning, the Garrett Mattingly book, is actually a book about the defeat of the Spanish Armada.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你所指出的，我们一开始读的那本书，加勒特·马廷利的那本书，实际上是一本关于击败西班牙无敌舰队的书。

sentences.en: So Spain and France are involved in this story too.
sentences.zh: 所以西班牙和法国也卷入了这场故事之中。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So actually, that account that you read, it's the first chapter in Mattingly's account of the Spanish Armada.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，你读的那段记载，是马廷利关于西班牙无敌舰队叙述的第一章。

sentences.en: He frames it as the key event that results in Philip II of Spain launching his doomed attempt to conquer England the following year in 1588.
sentences.zh: 他将其定性为关键事件，导致西班牙国王腓力二世在第二年（即1588年）发动了注定失败的征服英格兰的企图。

sentences.en: And that reflects the fact that throughout her life, Mary was a figure of absolutely European significance, and not just for Spain, but even more for France.
sentences.zh: 这反映了一个事实：在其一生中，玛丽一直是一个具有绝对欧洲意义的人物，不仅对西班牙如此，对法国而言更是如此。

sentences.en: So although she was the Queen of Scots, actually, I think the kingdom that she loved best, the place probably where she felt most at home was France.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管她是苏格兰女王，但实际上，我认为她最热爱的王国、大概也是她最感宾至如归的地方是法国。

sentences.en: So like, actually very like Theo, her father was Scottish, but her mother was French.
sentences.zh: 所以，实际上非常像西奥，她的父亲是苏格兰人，但她的母亲是法国人。

sentences.en: And she goes to, Theo just briefly flashed in and out there.
sentences.zh: 她去……西奥刚刚在那里一闪而过。

sentences.en: She goes to France when she's very young.
sentences.zh: 她很小的时候就去了法国。

sentences.en: She gets educated there.
sentences.zh: 她在那里接受教育。

sentences.en: She grows up there, where she first marries and becomes a queen.
sentences.zh: 她在那里长大，并在那里第一次结婚并成为王后。

sentences.en: And I think there's a sense in which all through her subsequent life, she's a little bit homesick for it.
sentences.zh: 我认为在某种程度上，在她随后的整个一生中，她都有点对那里感到思乡。

sentences.en: And so perhaps the great irony of her reign and the key to understanding her ultimate tragedy is that the preference of this most famous of all Scots wasn't actually for Scotland at all.
sentences.zh: 因此，她统治生涯中最大的讽刺、以及理解她最终悲剧的关键，或许在于这位所有苏格兰人中最著名的人，她真正偏爱的其实根本不是苏格兰。

sentences.en: Her heart was probably French.
sentences.zh: 她的心可能属于法国。

sentences.en: Enough preamble.
sentences.zh: 序言就到这里。

sentences.en: Let's get right into the story.
sentences.zh: 让我们直接切入正题。

sentences.en: So she is born in Linlithgow, west of Edinburgh, one of the great palaces of Scotland, on the 8th of December, 1542.
sentences.zh: 所以她于1542年12月8日出生在林利思戈，位于爱丁堡以西，是苏格兰伟大的宫殿之一。

sentences.en: So set the scene for us a little bit, Tom.
sentences.zh: 那么汤姆，请给我们稍微布置一下当时的场景。

sentences.en: It's perishingly cold, even by the standards of Scotland in winter.
sentences.zh: 那里冷得刺骨，即使以苏格兰冬天的标准来看也是如此。

sentences.en: So the Tweed, which is the fast flowing river on which I have my Scottish estate, and which marked the frontier between Scotland and England, had completely frozen over.
sentences.zh: 特威德河——那条我拥有苏格兰庄园的湍急河流，它曾是苏格兰和英格兰之间的国界——已经完全结冰了。

sentences.en: Which anyone who knows the Tweed, I mean, it's an extraordinary thing.
sentences.zh: 任何了解特威德河的人都会知道，我的意思是，这是一件非常了不起的事。

sentences.en: But despite these perishing conditions, it hasn't stopped the Scots and the English from fighting one another, which for generations after generation, they're always at it.
sentences.zh: 但尽管天气滴水成冰，但这并没有阻止苏格兰人和英格兰人互相厮杀，一代又一代的人，他们总是在打仗。

sentences.en: And this is why Mary's father, who is James V, he's 30 years old, he's the king of Scotland, that's why he's not present at Linlithgow for her birth.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么玛丽的父亲——詹姆斯五世，他30岁，是苏格兰国王——没有出席在林利思戈举行的她出生仪式的原因。

sentences.en: And the reason for this is that two weeks earlier, he'd been fighting the English on the western border of Scotland, and he had suffered a humiliating defeat,
sentences.zh: 原因在于，两周前他一直在苏格兰西部边界与英格兰人作战，并遭受了一场奇耻大辱的惨败，

sentences.en: Solway Moss in Cumberland, in England.
sentences.zh: 即英格兰坎布里亚郡的索尔韦莫斯之战。

sentences.en: He'd managed to escape the battlefield.
sentences.zh: 他设法逃离了战场。

sentences.en: He'd ridden back.
sentences.zh: 他骑马折返。

sentences.en: He'd stopped by at Linlithgow, where his wife had been entering her confinement.
sentences.zh: 他在林利思戈停留，当时他的妻子一直在那里待产。

sentences.en: But he hadn't stayed there, basically, I think, because he was kind of too depressed and miserable at his defeat.
sentences.zh: 但他并没有留下来，基本上，我认为是因为他因为战败而感到非常沮丧和痛苦。

sentences.en: He felt he had lots to organise.
sentences.zh: 他觉得自己有许多事情要安排。

sentences.en: So he went to Edinburgh.
sentences.zh: 所以他去了爱丁堡。

sentences.en: In Edinburgh, he felt, oh, I'm just too depressed.
sentences.zh: 在爱丁堡，他觉得，哦，我实在是太沮丧了。

sentences.en: And so he went on to a hunting lodge at Falkland.
sentences.zh: 于是他继续前往福克兰的一个狩猎小屋。

sentences.en: And basically, he seems to have gone there to commune with his sense of failure, I think.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他去那里似乎是为了沉浸在自己的失败感中，我想。

sentences.en: And he basically goes to bed.
sentences.zh: 他基本上就上床躺下了。

sentences.en: He's very depressed.
sentences.zh: 他非常沮丧。

sentences.en: He's also pox ridden.
sentences.zh: 他还染上了花柳病。

sentences.en: And he's a great one for the ladies and is absolutely ridden with syphilis.
sentences.zh: 他是个风流成性的人，浑身都染上了梅毒。

sentences.en: And while he's in bed, he has brought the news that his wife has given birth and it's a daughter.
sentences.zh: 正当他躺在床上时，传来了他妻子生下一个女儿的消息。

sentences.en: And this plunges him even deeper into misery.
sentences.zh: 这让他陷入了更深的痛苦之中。

sentences.en: Yeah, gutting.
sentences.zh: 是的，太令人痛心了。

sentences.en: Well, over the course of his life, as we will see, he's fathered a lot of bastard sons, but he has no legitimate male heir.
sentences.zh: 好吧，正如我们将看到的，在他的一生中，他生过许多私生子，但他没有合法的男性继承人。

sentences.en: And he'd really been hoping for that.
sentences.zh: 他真的非常渴望有一个儿子。

sentences.en: So having a daughter is a huge disappointment to him.
sentences.zh: 所以生个女儿对他是巨大的打击。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, back in Lithgow, the newborn daughter and her mother are doing very well.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在林利思戈，刚出生的女儿和她的母亲状况非常好。

sentences.en: And this is because a Scottish palace in the mid-16th century is actually an incredibly civilised place to be.
sentences.zh: 这是因为16世纪中叶的苏格兰宫殿实际上是一个极其文明的居住场所。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's great.
sentences.zh: 是的，这太棒了。

sentences.en: It's hung with magnificent tapestries to provide insulation.
sentences.zh: 里面挂着华丽的挂毯以提供保暖。

sentences.en: It's got the cutting edge glazed windows, tremendous glaziers on hand.
sentences.zh: 它有最先进的玻璃窗，手头有极好的玻璃匠。

sentences.en: It's very, very sophisticated.
sentences.zh: 它非常非常精致。

sentences.en: And in the opinion of Mary's mother, the palace at Linlithgow is the equal of any chateau to be found in France.
sentences.zh: 在玛丽的母亲看来，林利思戈宫不亚于法国的任何一座城堡。

sentences.en: She would know.
sentences.zh: 她对此自然心知肚明。

sentences.en: Absolutely, Dominic, because she herself is French.
sentences.zh: 没错，多米尼克，因为她本人就是法国人。

sentences.en: So she's Mary of Guise.
sentences.zh: 所以她是吉斯的玛丽。

sentences.en: She's from a noble family in France, right?
sentences.zh: 她来自法国的一个贵族家庭，对吧？

sentences.en: And she's famously beautiful and smart, cunning, all of these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 而且她以美貌、聪明、狡猾以及诸如此类的特质闻名。

sentences.en: And, I mean, no son.
sentences.zh: 再者，我是说，还没有儿子。

sentences.en: I mean, we're in the same century as Henry VIII and all his carry-on.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们身处的这个世纪正值亨利八世及其种种荒唐行径的年代。

sentences.en: So no son is, you know, always a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 所以没有儿子，你知道的，向来都不是件好事。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, at least James has an heir of a kind.
sentences.zh: 但从另一方面来看，至少詹姆斯有了一个某种意义上的继承人。

sentences.en: And you say she's of a noble family.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说她出身贵族世家。

sentences.en: I mean, the Guise are the most influential and domineering noble family in France.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，吉斯家族是法国最具影响力和专横跋扈的贵族。

sentences.en: And as we will see, they have essentially their eyes on the throne.
sentences.zh: 正如我们接下来将看到的，他们实际上对王位虎视眈眈。

sentences.en: So she's a very formidable person in her own right.
sentences.zh: 所以她本身就是一个非常了不起、令人敬畏的人物。

sentences.en: And her marriage to James V, the King of Scotland, it bears witness to what for generations and generations has been the foundation stone of Scotland's foreign policy,
sentences.zh: 她与苏格兰国王詹姆斯五世的联姻，见证了世世代代以来苏格兰外交政策的基石，

sentences.en: which is known by the Scots as the Old Alliance, A-U-L-D, so the Scots spelling.
sentences.zh: 被苏格兰人称为“老同盟”，拼法是A-U-L-D，采用的是苏格兰拼写。

sentences.en: And it is underpinned, I'm afraid to say, by a visceral hostility to England.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，这种同盟关系的支撑点是对英格兰发自内心的敌意。

sentences.en: Which makes complete sense.
sentences.zh: 这完全合乎情理。

sentences.en: I mean, strategically, England is the adversary for both countries.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从战略上讲，英格兰是这两个国家的共同对手。

sentences.en: The English had fought the French in the Hundred Years' War, memories of which are still around, obviously, in the 16th century.
sentences.zh: 英格兰人在百年战争中与法国人交战过，很显然，这些记忆在16世纪依然存在。

sentences.en: The Scots, so their memories are of their wars of independence, which were 300 years earlier.
sentences.zh: 而苏格兰人，他们的记忆则是关于早了300年的独立战争。

sentences.en: Robert the Bruce, all of that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·布鲁斯，以及所有诸如此类的事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And actually, both of these had been English defeats, hadn't they?
sentences.zh: 而且实际上，这些战争都是英格兰人的惨败，不是吗？

sentences.en: They had.
sentences.zh: 的确如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The English defeat in the Scottish wars of independence had been much more humiliating for the English than their defeat in the Hundred Years' War.
sentences.zh: 英格兰人在苏格兰独立战争中的失败，比他们在百年战争中的失败要耻辱得多。

sentences.en: Basically, because Scotland is to England what England is to France, namely, less rich, less powerful, fewer reserves of manpower.
sentences.zh: 基本上是因为苏格兰对英格兰而言，就像英格兰对法国一样，也就是更不富裕、力量更弱、人力储备更少。

sentences.en: And this is as true in the time of Mary, Queen of Scots, as it had been back in the time of Robert Bruce.
sentences.zh: 在苏格兰女王玛丽的时代，情况如此，在罗伯特·布鲁斯的时代也是如此。

sentences.en: So, the population of England is about three and a half million.
sentences.zh: 所以，英格兰的人口大约是三百五十万。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Scotland's is well under one million.
sentences.zh: 而苏格兰的人口则远远不到一百万。

sentences.en: The only sizable town in Scotland at this time is Edinburgh.
sentences.zh: 这个时期苏格兰唯一初具规模的城镇就是爱丁堡。

sentences.en: Even then, I mean, it's only just under 10,000.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，我是说，它也仅仅不到一万人。

sentences.en: So, London, by way of comparison, is over 60,000.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，伦敦的人口超过了六万。

sentences.en: And its entire machinery of government is much less centralised than you get in England or France.
sentences.zh: 而且整个政府机器远没有英格兰或法国那么集权。

sentences.en: And so, therefore, it's harder to raise and sustain armies in the field.
sentences.zh: 因此，要在战场上召集和维持军队也就更加困难。

sentences.en: And the corollary of that is that generally, provided the English aren't distracted by kind of wars in France, they can pretty much be relied upon to defeat the Scots in battle.
sentences.zh: 其必然结果是，一般来说，只要英格兰人不被法国的战事所分心，基本上就可以断定他们能在战斗中击败苏格兰人。

sentences.en: As they have done in recent years, right?
sentences.zh: 正如他们近年来所做的那样，对吧？

sentences.en: So, the 16th century has been pretty good for England in this regard.
sentences.zh: 所以，就这一点而言，16世纪对英格兰来说相当不错。

sentences.en: You mentioned Solway Moss, but they also famously won the Battle of Flodden, 1513.
sentences.zh: 你提到了索尔韦苔原之战，但他们同样以在1513年赢得弗洛登战役而闻名。

sentences.en: A lot of business with pikemen running down into bogs and things.
sentences.zh: 有许多长枪兵冲进泥沼之类的混乱场面。

sentences.en: And Mary's grandfather was killed at Flodden, wasn't he, James IV?
sentences.zh: 玛丽的祖父詹姆斯四世就是在弗洛登战役中战死的，对吧？

sentences.en: And a lot of the English people said that he'd been killed by his own side, which is poor from the Scots.
sentences.zh: 许多英格兰人说他是死于自己人之手，这苏格兰人可真逊。

sentences.en: Well, I think not just English people, Scots thought that too.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为不仅是英格兰人，苏格兰人也这么认为。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's unclear.
sentences.zh: 目前还不清楚。

sentences.en: But these rumours certainly play into a kind of opinion that is very common in England and indeed France.
sentences.zh: 但这些传言无疑迎合了一种在英格兰乃至法国都极为普遍的观点。

sentences.en: That Scottish affairs are exceptionally brutal and murderous.
sentences.zh: 即苏格兰事务极其残暴、充满谋杀。

sentences.en: And that the nobility in Scotland are kind of very, very thuggish and dangerous.
sentences.zh: 并且苏格兰的贵族阶层非常蛮横凶残且危险。

sentences.en: Do you think it's true?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Well, we'll see.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们拭目以待。

sentences.en: Mary certainly grows up to think it's true.
sentences.zh: 玛丽长大后绝对是这么认为的。

sentences.en: In due course, she would say of the Scots that they are, as is known, a people as factious amongst themselves and as factious towards their ruler as any other nation in Europe.
sentences.zh: 后来，她曾这样评价苏格兰人：众所周知，他们是一个无论在内部还是对统治者而言，都如同欧洲任何其他国家一样充满党争的民族。

sentences.en: And I guess that, you know, she could look back at her forebears, those who had sat on the throne before her and found plenty of evidence to support this.
sentences.zh: 我想，她可以回顾她的先辈们，那些曾坐在她之前的王位上的人，并能找到大量的证据来支持这一点。

sentences.en: So Mary is a steward.
sentences.zh: 所以玛丽是一位斯图尔特。

sentences.en: The name steward derives from the position held by one of her ancestors, who'd been the high steward of Scotland.
sentences.zh: “斯图尔特”这个名字源于她的一位祖先所担任的职务，他曾担任苏格兰高级总管。

sentences.en: And he had then married the daughter of Robert Bruce, a woman called Marjorie, which I think is an improbable name for a Scottish queen, and thereby founded the Stuart dynasty.
sentences.zh: 后来他娶了罗伯特·布鲁斯的女儿，一个名叫玛乔丽的女子——我认为这作为苏格兰王后的名字有点不太可能——并由此创立了斯图尔特王朝。

sentences.en: And it's true that very few of the Stuart kings kind of die in their beds.
sentences.zh: 事实也的确如此，很少有斯图尔特国王能寿终正寝。

sentences.en: So there are lots who die in battle against the English, but there's another who gets assassinated while being pursued down a sewer.
sentences.zh: 有许多人在对阵英格兰人的战斗中战死，但还有人在沿下水道逃跑时遭人暗杀。

sentences.en: Another gets killed in battle fighting his own son.
sentences.zh: 另有一个人在与自己亲生儿子的战斗中丧生。

sentences.en: And actually, the son who kills his own father is the guy who goes on to become James IV, the one who dies at Flodden.
sentences.zh: 事实上，杀死亲生父亲的那个儿子后来成为了詹姆斯四世，也就是死于弗洛登战役的那位。

sentences.en: So I think there is a general sense that to be a Scottish monarch is a dangerous thing.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为普遍的看法是，当苏格兰君主是一件危险的事。

sentences.en: And this, I think, is why James is particularly depressed at the news that he's been given a daughter rather than a son,
sentences.zh: 我认为，这就是为什么詹姆斯听到自己得到的不是儿子而是女儿的消息时会如此沮丧，

sentences.en: because he's worried that to have a woman on the throne will, by its very nature, be threatening, not just for Scotland, but more specifically for his own line, his own regime.
sentences.zh: 因为他担心王位上有一个女人，其本身就会构成威胁，不仅对苏格兰，而且更具体地说是对他自己的血脉、他自己的政权而言。

sentences.en: He has this brilliant line, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他有一句非常精彩的话，对吧？

sentences.en: The devil go with it.
sentences.zh: 让魔鬼随它去吧。

sentences.en: It will end as it began.
sentences.zh: 它将以开始的方式结束。

sentences.en: And it came from a woman and it will end in a woman.
sentences.zh: 它因一个女人而开始，也将以一个女人而告终。

sentences.en: What's all that about?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's kind of paraphrased.
sentences.zh: 是的，这其实是一种意译。

sentences.en: It came with a lass and it will pass with a lass.
sentences.zh: 它随一个丫头而来，也将随一个丫头消逝。

sentences.en: So in other words, the Stuarts inherited the throne via Marjorie, the daughter of Robert Bruce.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，斯图尔特家族是通过罗伯特·布鲁斯的女儿玛乔丽继承了王位。

sentences.en: And with Mary Stuart, it will finish.
sentences.zh: 而随着玛丽·斯图尔特，这一切将画上句号。

sentences.en: And so he's very depressed.
sentences.zh: 所以他感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: It gets worse and worse.
sentences.zh: 情况变得越来越糟糕。

sentences.en: And then he dies.
sentences.zh: 然后他死了。

sentences.en: And we're told by someone who records the details that he died amid a marvellous vomit.
sentences.zh: 记录细节的人告诉我们，他是在一场惊人的呕吐中死去的。

sentences.en: So, ooh, horrid.
sentences.zh: 所以，哦，太可怕了。

sentences.en: And so this is one week after Mary has been born.
sentences.zh: 而这正是玛丽出生一周后发生的事。

sentences.en: And so she's now the Queen of Scotland and she is one week old.
sentences.zh: 所以她现在是苏格兰女王，而她才刚刚出生一周。

sentences.en: And obviously, if the stereotypes, which very strongly held by foreigners, but also it would seem by James V himself,
sentences.zh: 很显然，如果外国人笃信的那些刻板印象——詹姆斯五世本人似乎也深信不疑——

sentences.en: if the stereotypes of Scottish savagery and backwardness are true, then you would think that the Stuarts are doomed.
sentences.zh: 如果关于苏格兰野蛮和落后的刻板印象是真的，那么你就会觉得斯图尔特家族命运休矣。

sentences.en: You know, a one week old baby girl on the throne.
sentences.zh: 你想想，一个出生才一周的女婴坐在王位上。

sentences.en: It doesn't look promising.
sentences.zh: 这看起来毫无希望。

sentences.en: And even more threatening is the fact that there are a couple of noblemen on the scene who themselves have a possible claim to the throne and who even more threateningly for Scotland absolutely test each other.
sentences.zh: 而更具威胁的是，当时现场有几个贵族，他们本身对王位也有继承权，而且对苏格兰来说更具威胁的是，他们彼此深恶痛绝。

sentences.en: Everybody basically is called James.
sentences.zh: 基本上每个人都叫詹姆斯。

sentences.en: So one of these is James Hamilton and he is the Earl of Arran.
sentences.zh: 其中一人叫詹姆斯·汉密尔顿，他是阿伦伯爵。

sentences.en: And he is the grandson of the daughter of James II.
sentences.zh: 他是詹姆斯二世女儿的孙子。

sentences.en: So that's going quite a few generations back.
sentences.zh: 所以这要追溯到好几代以前。

sentences.en: But he is now the heir apparent.
sentences.zh: 但他现在是法定继承人。

sentences.en: So if Mary dies, he gets the throne.
sentences.zh: 因此如果玛丽死了，他就能得到王位。

sentences.en: He's very scheming, but he's also very slippery and very, very inconstant.
sentences.zh: 他诡计多端，但也极其滑头、反复无常。

sentences.en: And Mary of Guise, Mary, Queen of Scotland's mother, despises him.
sentences.zh: 而苏格兰女王玛丽的母亲吉斯的玛丽，对他鄙视至极。

sentences.en: And she says of him that he was a simple and the most inconstant man in the world for whatever he determineth today, he changeth tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 她评价他说，他是一个单纯且世界上最反复无常的人，今天决定的事情，明天就会改变。

sentences.en: So you can't pin him down.
sentences.zh: 所以你根本捉摸不透他。

sentences.en: And the other bloke?
sentences.zh: 那另一个人呢？

sentences.en: So he is called Matthew, Matthew Stuart, and he's the Earl of Lennox.
sentences.zh: 他叫马修，马修·斯图尔特，是伦诺克斯伯爵。

sentences.en: And like the Earl of Arran, he's a grandson of James II's daughter.
sentences.zh: 和阿伦伯爵一样，他是詹姆斯二世女儿的孙子。

sentences.en: But he stands behind Arran in the ranking because his claim derives from a female rather than a male line.
sentences.zh: 但他在继承权排名中排在阿伦之后，因为他的继承权来自女性血脉而非男性血脉。

sentences.en: So the inherent sexism of the Scottish laws of inheritance.
sentences.zh: 这就是苏格兰继承法中固有的性别歧视。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he is in exile in France at this time when Mary is born, but he's obviously itching to return.
sentences.zh: 玛丽出生时，他正在法国流亡，但他显然急于返回。

sentences.en: And he's described by one admirer as having been a strong man of personage, well proportioned in all his members.
sentences.zh: 一位崇拜者这样描述他：身材魁梧，各部位比例匀称。

sentences.en: So that's nice.
sentences.zh: 这倒挺好。

sentences.en: In all his members.
sentences.zh: 各部位都很匀称。

sentences.en: That's nice.
sentences.zh: 这挺不错的。

sentences.en: Potentially a very impressive figure.
sentences.zh: 潜在的非常威严的人物。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So in a sane world, one of these men would have got the baby, taken her to some equivalent of the Tower of London, Scottish equivalent, some shack in Scotland,
sentences.zh: 所以在理智的世界里，其中一个人本该抓住这个婴儿，把她带到伦敦塔的同类地方、苏格兰的同类地方，比如苏格兰的某个窝棚，

sentences.en: and smothered or otherwise dealt with her.
sentences.zh: 然后将其闷死或用其他方式除掉。

sentences.en: This isn't a Tower style.
sentences.zh: 这不是伦敦塔的风格。

sentences.en: Bang.
sentences.zh: 砰。

sentences.en: Job done.
sentences.zh: 大功告成。

sentences.en: Let's get on and have a nice stable government for a happier Scotland.
sentences.zh: 让我们继续，为一个更幸福的苏格兰建立一个美好的稳定政府。

sentences.en: But no.
sentences.zh: 然而并没有。

sentences.en: Forage from the Scots.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰人可不这么干。

sentences.en: They could have done it and they would have been right to do it, I guess, would be definitely your take on it.
sentences.zh: 他们本可以这么做，而且照你的看法，他们这么做绝对是正确的，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But actually, this doesn't happen at all.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，这一切根本没有发生。

sentences.en: And this is because, actually, Scotland is much more politically stable, I think, than the negative perspective abroad allowed.
sentences.zh: 这是因为，实际上苏格兰的政治稳定性比国外那些悲观的看法所承认的要高得多。

sentences.en: And the measure of this is that since 1437, so that's more than a century before Mary's birth, four kings in succession had come to the Scottish throne as children.
sentences.zh: 衡量这一点的标准是，自1437年以来——也就是玛丽出生前一个多世纪——先后有四位国王在孩童时期登上苏格兰王位。

sentences.en: And all of them had survived their minority and all of them had grown up to become very powerful and intimidating rulers.
sentences.zh: 他们所有人都熬过了未成年时期，并且都长大成为了非常强大、令人畏惧的统治者。

sentences.en: And the reason for this is that, actually, the Scottish monarchy has a number of advantages that aren't immediately apparent, I think, to, you know, sneer us in London or Paris.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，实际上苏格兰君主制拥有许多优势，这些优势对于伦敦或巴黎那些冷嘲热讽的人来说，并不是那么显而易见。

sentences.en: And one of these advantages is that, actually, the aristocracy are not as feral as, say,
sentences.zh: 其中一个优势是，实际上贵族阶层并没有像……那样彻底失控

sentences.en: the English aristocracy had shown themselves to be in the 15th century when England had collapsed into the Wars of the Roses.
sentences.zh: 英格兰贵族在15世纪英格兰陷入玫瑰战争时所表现出的那样。

sentences.en: And, as you mentioned, the princess and the tower end up being murdered.
sentences.zh: 正如你所提到的，王子和塔楼的遭遇最终是被谋杀。

sentences.en: There's no equivalent of that in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰没有与之相当的事件。

sentences.en: And Jenny Wormald, who we mentioned, the great historian of late medieval and 16th century Scotland, who's very down on Mary, Queen of Scots,
sentences.zh: 我们提到过的詹妮·沃尔马尔德，她是晚期中世纪和16世纪苏格兰的伟大历史学家，她对苏格兰女王玛丽持严厉批评态度，

sentences.en: she's brilliant on this kind of quality of essential stability that Scotland has.
sentences.zh: 她在探讨苏格兰这种内在稳定性的品质时表现得极为出色。

sentences.en: And she writes, the evidence is that the magnates infinitely preferred strong royal rule to lack of it.
sentences.zh: 她写道：种种迹象表明，权贵们无限倾向于强有力的皇家统治，而非没有统治。

sentences.en: So they're not looking to overthrow kings.
sentences.zh: 所以他们并不寻求推翻国王。

sentences.en: Essentially, they want a king to grow up and provide authoritative rule because that's...
sentences.zh: 本质上，他们希望国王长大并提供权威的统治，因为那是……

sentences.en: Better for Scotland.
sentences.zh: 对苏格兰更好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they're doing that partly because they're frightened of the English or they're not frightened of the English.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做部分是因为他们害怕英格兰人，或者说他们不害怕英格兰人？

sentences.en: I think they are constantly aware of the English threat on their southern border.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们始终意识到南部边境来自英格兰的威胁。

sentences.en: They're well aware that in pitch battle, the English are probably going to win.
sentences.zh: 他们非常清楚，在正面交锋中，英格兰人很可能会获胜。

sentences.en: But they're also aware that as long as there is a strong, stable state in Scotland, the English will never be able to conquer Scotland.
sentences.zh: 但他们也明白，只要苏格兰存在一个强大、稳定的国家，英格兰人就永远无法征服苏格兰。

sentences.en: The Highlands, in particular, are effectively impregnable.
sentences.zh: 尤其是高地，几乎是攻不可破的。

sentences.en: You know, it's not just the English who failed to conquer Scotland.
sentences.zh: 要知道，不仅仅是英格兰人没能征服苏格兰。

sentences.en: And the Romans had failed earlier.
sentences.zh: 罗马人早些时候也失败了。

sentences.en: It's just Scotland is a very, very difficult country to subdue.
sentences.zh: 只是苏格兰是一个非常非常难以征服的国家。

sentences.en: And so as a result, the English are kind of like a tide.
sentences.zh: 因此，英格兰人就像潮水一样。

sentences.en: They're constantly flowing in, but they're almost bound to flow back out again.
sentences.zh: 他们不断涌入，但几乎注定要退回去。

sentences.en: And this is why ever since Edward I tried to conquer Scotland and Edward II had then been defeated at Bannockburn,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么自从爱德华一世试图征服苏格兰、而爱德华二世随后在班诺克本战役中被击败以来，

sentences.en: it's just a relentless sequence of wars and squabbles that are never resolved.
sentences.zh: 这只是一连串永无休止、从未解决的战争和争吵。

sentences.en: The Scots can't stop the English attacking, but the English can't subdue the Scots.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰人无法阻止英格兰人的进攻，但英格兰人也无法征服苏格兰人。

sentences.en: And so you just have this kind of three centuries long stalemate.
sentences.zh: 所以你们只能看到这种长达三个世纪的僵局。

sentences.en: One of the reasons that the Scots are able to see the English off is that actually in kind of geopolitical terms, they're quite well set.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰人能够击退英格兰人的原因之一是，实际上从地缘政治的角度来看，他们的处境相当不错。

sentences.en: So if you think of France, France has the English to deal with, but they've also got the Spanish.
sentences.zh: 如果你想想法国，法国不仅要对付英格兰人，还要应付西班牙人。

sentences.en: They've got problems on the Italian frontier.
sentences.zh: 他们在意大利边境也有麻烦。

sentences.en: They've been fighting in Italy, yeah.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在意大利打仗，对吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, they've got Italy, they've got the Low Countries, they've got problems potentially along the Rhine.
sentences.zh: 对，他们占领了意大利，占领了低地国家，在莱茵河沿岸可能还有潜在的麻烦。

sentences.en: So they have enemies on almost every corner.
sentences.zh: 所以他们几乎在每个角落都有敌人。

sentences.en: The English are sandwiched between France and Scotland.
sentences.zh: 英格兰夹在法国和苏格兰之间。

sentences.en: So whenever the English go and attack France, as Shakespeare puts it, the weasel Scot darts out down into northern England.
sentences.zh: 因此，每当英格兰人去攻打法国时，正如莎士比亚所说，那个狡猾的苏格兰人就会溜进英格兰北部。

sentences.en: The Scots only have the one natural enemy, and that's England.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰人只有一个天然的敌人，那就是英格兰。

sentences.en: And this is one of the reasons why it doesn't actually need the centralised bureaucracy that had developed in England and France.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么它其实并不需要英格兰和法国那种发展起来的中央集权官僚体制的一个原因。

sentences.en: They can't say over the course of the Hundred Years' War.
sentences.zh: 他们可不能在百年战争期间这么说。

sentences.en: They don't need excessive amounts of money or men,
sentences.zh: 他们不需要过多的金钱或兵力，

sentences.en: because the only sphere where they're going to be fighting is that very narrow border that constitutes the line between England and France.
sentences.zh: 因为他们唯一要战斗的领域就是构成英格兰和法国分界线的那个非常狭窄的边界。

sentences.en: And so such taxes as they raise, the Stuarts can blow it on fancy ships or guns, and they love a fancy ship.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们征收的那些税款，斯图亚特王朝可以挥霍在花哨的船只或大炮上，而且他们非常喜欢豪华的船只。

sentences.en: They love a massive cannon, but they can still have enough to then spend it on building glorious palaces like at Linlithgow.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢巨大的大炮，但他们依然能有足够的资金用来建造像林利思戈那样金碧辉煌的宫殿。

sentences.en: So this is why you have the wonderful glazing and the tapestries and stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么会有精美的玻璃窗、挂毯以及诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: It's because the Scottish monarchy has money to spare.
sentences.zh: 那是因为苏格兰君主有富余的资金。

sentences.en: Basically, James V is a great builder of kind of the Scottish equivalent of Chateau.
sentences.zh: 基本上，詹姆斯五世是个建造城堡的行家，相当于苏格兰版的城堡修建者。

sentences.en: He can enjoy French-style interior decoration, but massively on the cheap.
sentences.zh: 他可以享受法式风格的室内装饰，而且成本极低。

sentences.en: And because of this, the Scots themselves do not feel that they're peripheral barbarians.
sentences.zh: 正因为如此，苏格兰人自己并不觉得自己是边缘蛮族。

sentences.en: And the Scots monarchs certainly don't think that.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰君主当然更不会这么想。

sentences.en: They don't see themselves as being remote or isolated or backwards.
sentences.zh: 他们不觉得自己偏远、孤立或落后。

sentences.en: They see themselves absolutely as being the peers of the King of England or the King of France.
sentences.zh: 他们绝对把自己看作是与英格兰国王或法国国王平起平坐的人。

sentences.en: And so that's why I think, although it's not optimal to have a one-week-old baby girl on the throne,
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么我认为，尽管让一个出生才一周的女婴登上王位并不是最优的选择，

sentences.en: it doesn't doom Mary, and it doesn't mean that Scotland is doomed to fall to pieces.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有给玛丽判死刑，也不意味着苏格兰注定要四分五裂。

sentences.en: Well, let's find out, because, you know, Tom, that's very optimistic.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们拭目以待，因为你知道的，汤姆，这太乐观了。

sentences.en: Are we looking for a golden age of Scottish history?
sentences.zh: 我们在期待苏格兰历史上的一个黄金时代吗？

sentences.en: Is Mary, Queen of Scots life, going to be all sweetness and light?
sentences.zh: 苏格兰女王玛丽的一生，难道会是一帆风顺、充满美好吗？

sentences.en: Find out after the break.
sentences.zh: 广告之后为您揭晓。

sentences.zh: 大博弈，英国和俄罗斯之间的战略博弈。

sentences.en: We assess, uh, Prime Minister, with high confidence it was Russian.
sentences.zh: 我们评估，呃，首相，我们高度确信这是俄罗斯干的。

sentences.en: Holding the Russians accountable is World War III.
sentences.zh: 追究俄罗斯人的责任就等于第三次世界大战。

sentences.en: They took down a British passenger jet containing 350 people.
sentences.zh: 他们击落了一架载有350人的英国客机。

sentences.zh: 克里姆林宫的那位在下棋，亚历克斯。

sentences.zh: 你得问问自己，你到底想不想玩？

sentences.zh: 你什么都没做！

sentences.zh: 我们需要理解政策背景。

sentences.en: A frago that says to kill the president of Russia.
sentences.zh: 一份要求干掉俄罗斯总统的作战指令。
