sentences.en: Welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史的其余部分》。

sentences.en: Now, if you're not a member of The Rest is History Club, I know what you've been doing.
sentences.zh: 好了，如果你还不是“历史的其余部分”俱乐部成员，我知道你刚才都在干什么。

sentences.en: You've been listening to the adverts.
sentences.zh: 你一直在听广告。

sentences.en: More fool you.
sentences.zh: 你可真傻。

sentences.en: You should join the club and you won't have to listen to them.
sentences.zh: 你早就该加入俱乐部的，这样就不用听广告了。

sentences.en: But while you've been listening to the adverts, extraordinary scenes.
sentences.zh: 但就在你听广告的时候，发生了极其惊人的场景。

sentences.en: Nine months have passed, and Mary has just been crowned in Stirling Castle.
sentences.zh: 九个月过去了，玛丽刚刚在斯特林城堡加冕。

sentences.en: A slightly bad omen here, Tom, because she was crowned on the anniversary of the Battle of Flodden.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这似乎是个不太吉利的预兆，因为她加冕的日子正好是弗洛登战役的周年纪念日。

sentences.en: Yeah, so the 9th of September, 1543, 29 years after the Battle of Flodden.
sentences.zh: 对，也就是1543年9月9日，弗洛登战役发生的29年后。

sentences.en: So, big disaster in Scottish history.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是苏格兰历史上的一大灾难。

sentences.en: Why on earth have they chosen that date?
sentences.zh: 他们到底为什么要选这个日子？

sentences.en: Well, it will be seen by Mary's enemies as a bad omen.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在玛丽的敌人看来，这会被视为一个不祥之兆。

sentences.en: But I think you could just as easily see it as a mark of Scottish insouciance.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你同样可以把它看作是苏格兰人漫不经心、无所畏惧的表现。

sentences.en: They've already got over Flodden.
sentences.zh: 他们早就把弗洛登战役抛在脑后了。

sentences.en: Forget it.
sentences.zh: 忘掉它吧。

sentences.en: You know, yeah, who cares?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，没错，谁在乎呢？

sentences.en: As you said, she's crowned in Stirling Castle, which has always been viewed as the key to Scotland.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，她是在斯特林城堡加冕的，这里一直被视为苏格兰的钥匙。

sentences.en: Bannockburn is kind of fought in its shadow.
sentences.zh: 班诺克战役可以说就是在它的阴影下进行的。

sentences.en: It guards the lowest crossing point on the River Forth, and it's pretty much impregnable.
sentences.zh: 它守卫着福斯河上下游交汇的最低渡口，而且几乎坚不可摧。

sentences.en: So, that is one of the reasons why Mary is there.
sentences.zh: 所以，这也是玛丽选择在那里的原因之一。

sentences.en: The crown has to be held over the baby queen's head, because obviously it would crush her if it was laid on top of her.
sentences.zh: 王冠必须举在小女王头顶上方，因为很显然，如果直接戴在她头上会把她压垮的。

sentences.en: And Mary cries and bawls and sobs the whole way through the ceremony.
sentences.zh: 而且玛丽在整个加冕典礼过程中一直在哭喊、大哭和啜泣。

sentences.en: Which, again, people might see as an omen.
sentences.zh: 这同样可能会被人们视为一个不祥之兆。

sentences.en: But, you know, very clearly, if she's being crowned, she hasn't been murdered.
sentences.zh: 但是，很显然，既然她正在加冕，说明她并没有被谋杀。

sentences.en: Coronation is going ahead.
sentences.zh: 加冕礼正在顺利进行。

sentences.en: The country hasn't collapsed into civil war.
sentences.zh: 国家也没有陷入内战。

sentences.en: And great news, the earls of Arran and Lennox, so the two men who we mentioned in the first half, who both have claims to be her successor, they've been there.
sentences.zh: 而且有个好消息，阿兰伯爵和伦诺克斯伯爵，也就是我们在前半部分提到的那两个人，他们两个都对王位继承权提出过主张，他们都出席了。

sentences.en: So, the first one, massive snake.
sentences.zh: 所以，第一个家伙，简直是个彻头彻尾的阴险小人。

sentences.en: Yeah, always changing his mind.
sentences.zh: 对，总是朝秦暮楚。

sentences.en: The other bloke.
sentences.zh: 另一个家伙。

sentences.en: Good members.
sentences.zh: 身体很健壮。

sentences.en: Well-proportioned members, yeah.
sentences.zh: 身材比例很好的成员，对吧。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, Arran has carried the crown in the coronation procession.
sentences.zh: 因此，阿兰在加冕游行中抬着王冠。

sentences.en: Lennox has carried the scepter.
sentences.zh: 伦诺克斯则手持权杖。

sentences.en: If you throw in the sword of state as well, these constitute the honours of Scotland, as they're called.
sentences.zh: 如果你再把国剑算上，这些就是所谓的苏格兰国宝。

sentences.en: And you can see them to this day in Edinburgh Castle.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，你还能在爱丁堡城堡里看到它们。

sentences.en: Attentive listeners may remember that Lennox had been in exile in France.
sentences.zh: 细心的听众可能还记得，伦诺克斯之前一直在法国流亡。

sentences.en: So, obviously, if he's there in Stirling, he's negotiated his return.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，既然他出现在斯特林，说明他已经通过谈判回国了。

sentences.en: So, it's good for him.
sentences.zh: 这对他是好事。

sentences.en: But it's Arran probably, at this point, who is ahead because he has won the backing of Scotland's parliament to serve both as regent and to be nominated as Mary's official heir.
sentences.zh: 但此时占上风的可能还是阿兰，因为他赢得了苏格兰议会的支持，既担任摄政王，又被指定为玛丽的官方继承人。

sentences.en: So, yeah, watch out for him.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，提防着点他。

sentences.en: If he had a Richard III vibe, we know what would happen.
sentences.zh: 如果他带有一点理查三世的气质，我们都知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But we will see.
sentences.zh: 但我们拭目以待。

sentences.en: In one sense, there's a kind of surprising degree of political stability.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这里的政治稳定程度高得令人惊讶。

sentences.en: These two earls are kind of, you know, they're eyeballing each other, but they're not trying to kill Mary.
sentences.zh: 这两个伯爵虽然都在互相打量对方，但他们并没有试图谋杀玛丽。

sentences.en: They're not in open opposition to one another.
sentences.zh: 他们彼此之间并没有公开对抗。

sentences.en: But the state of Scotland is unsettled even so.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，苏格兰的局势仍然动荡不安。

sentences.en: And this is due not so much to the rivalry between Arran and Lennox, but to a much more formidable and enduring rivalry, which is that between France and England.
sentences.zh: 这与其说是由于阿兰和伦诺克斯之间的竞争，不如说是由于一场更强大、更持久的竞争，那就是法国和英格兰之间的竞争。

sentences.en: So, both of those kingdoms, they've obviously heard the news.
sentences.zh: 因此，这两个王国显然都听到了这个消息。

sentences.en: There's this infant girl and they're both thinking, oh, you know, there's opportunity here.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个婴儿女孩，他们都在想，哦，你知道的，这里有机可乘。

sentences.en: Now, you would think, wouldn't you, that the French would be the people who would do a deal with Scotland because of the old alliance and all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能会想，鉴于历史上的老同盟以及诸如此类的关系，法国人应该是那个会与苏格兰达成协议的人吧。

sentences.en: And the English are kind of the, you know, they're the old enemy and all of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 而英格兰人算是那种老敌人，诸如此类的。

sentences.en: And it's a little bit more complicated, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但事情要复杂得多，对吧？

sentences.en: So, the English are actually at war with Scotland at this point, technically.
sentences.zh: 所以，从技术层面上讲，英格兰目前实际上正与苏格兰交战。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, Mary's father died of a broken heart after being defeated by them.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我的意思是，玛丽的父亲在被他们击败后心碎而死。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, of course, also, Mary is under the wing of her mother, Mary of Guise, who's very much a French woman.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有玛丽在她的母亲吉斯的玛丽的羽翼下，而她母亲是个地地道道的法国女人。

sentences.en: So, why is this even an issue?
sentences.zh: 所以，这怎么还能算是个问题呢？

sentences.en: Why the English, even in play, is a possible ally?
sentences.zh: 为什么英格兰甚至会被考虑作为一个可能的盟友？

sentences.en: It doesn't make sense.
sentences.zh: 这根本说不通。

sentences.en: Over the decade before Mary is born, something very kind of novel, unexpected, and I think for relations between Scotland, England, and France,
sentences.zh: 在玛丽出生前的十年里，某种非常新颖、出乎意料，而且我认为对于苏格兰、英格兰和法国之间的关系来说，

sentences.en: very destabilizing has begun to emerge, which is a pro-English faction in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 极其具有破坏性的因素开始显现出来，那就是苏格兰出现了一个亲英派阵营。

sentences.en: Absolute scenes.
sentences.zh: 简直是活久见。

sentences.en: I mean, unheard of.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，闻所未闻。

sentences.en: So, people may wonder, how on earth is it that a pro-English faction has grown up in Scotland?
sentences.zh: 所以人们可能会好奇，苏格兰怎么会突然冒出一个亲英派阵营呢？

sentences.en: And the answer to that is that the storm clouds of the Reformation have been massing, not just over Europe, but over Scotland.
sentences.zh: 答案是，宗教改革的阴云不仅在欧洲上空聚集，也在苏格兰上空聚集。

sentences.en: Because, just as has been happening in England at the same time, the country is being shaken by the emergence of a novel and very fast-growing heresy in Germany.
sentences.zh: 因为，正如英格兰同时发生的情况一样，这个国家正因德国涌现出一种新颖且快速蔓延的异端邪说而受到震动。

sentences.en: So, we did five episodes on this, the life of Martin Luther, kind of the father of the Reformation.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们为此做了五集节目，讲述马丁·路德的一生，他可以说是宗教改革之父。

sentences.en: And his writings had been detected in Scotland as early as 1524.
sentences.zh: 早在1524年，他的著作就在苏格兰被发现了。

sentences.en: So, that's only a few years after he nailed up his theses in Wittenberg.
sentences.zh: 那也就是他在维滕贝格贴出他的《九十五条论纲》之后短短几年时间。

sentences.en: And then three years later, so in 1527, there is a report from a concerned Catholic that Luther's writings are circulating widely in Edinburgh and St. Andrews.
sentences.zh: 然后三年后，也就是1527年，一位担忧的天主教徒报告说，路德的著作正在爱丁堡和圣安德鲁斯广泛流传。

sentences.en: And then the following year, in 1528, you get the first martyrdom of a Protestant.
sentences.zh: 接着在第二年，即1528年，发生了第一起新教徒殉道事件。

sentences.en: And this is a former Catholic priest called Patrick Hamilton.
sentences.zh: 这是一个名叫帕特里克·汉密尔顿的前天主教神父。

sentences.en: And he's burnt at the stake in St. Andrews, which is one of Scotland's three universities at this point, and the oldest and most prestigious.
sentences.zh: 他在圣安德鲁斯被火刑处死，圣安德鲁斯是当时苏格兰的三所大学之一，也是历史最悠久、声誉最高的一所。

sentences.en: So, this is all going on.
sentences.zh: 所以，这一切都在发生。

sentences.en: But surely there's a huge thing.
sentences.zh: 但肯定有一件大事。

sentences.en: It's not just coming from Germany or from Flanders or other places the tracts are coming from.
sentences.zh: 这些小册子不仅仅来自德国、佛兰德斯或其他地方。

sentences.en: But the fact that England has been embroiled in the Reformation because of Henry VIII's marital issues, presumably has a massive knock-on effect on Scotland.
sentences.zh: 由于亨利八世的婚姻问题，英格兰卷入了宗教改革，这一事实想必对苏格兰产生了巨大的连锁反应。

sentences.en: Because now, all sorts of tracts and ideas can arrive across the very porous Anglo-Scottish border.
sentences.zh: 因为现在，各种小册子和思想可以通过极其千疮百孔的英苏边境涌入进来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And, of course, they're written in a form of English.
sentences.zh: 而且，它们当然是用某种形式的英语写的。

sentences.en: So, Scots, which is pretty different from the kind of English that is being written by Protestant reformers in London or Cambridge or whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以，苏格兰语与伦敦或剑桥等地的宗教改革者所写的英语有很大不同。

sentences.en: But, I mean, it's much easier for Scots to read than, say, German.
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，苏格兰人读起来比读德语要容易得多。

sentences.en: And so, these pamphlets have an outsized effect on Scottish opinion, as you said.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这些小册子对苏格兰的舆论产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: And, of course, as you also said, there is the outsized figure of Henry VIII.
sentences.zh: 而且，正如你刚才也提到的，还有一个极其显眼的人物——亨利八世。

sentences.en: And by this point, I mean, he really is outsized.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候，我的意思是，他的身材确实大得惊人。

sentences.en: He's very much a person of bulk.
sentences.zh: 他是个体形非常庞大的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's got that massive ulcer.
sentences.zh: 对，他身上长了个巨大的溃疡。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: All those injections up his arse and stuff.
sentences.zh: 屁股上还要做各种注射之类的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's all happening.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，各种状况不断。

sentences.en: So, his kind of beady, piggy little eyes have lit up at the prospect that the spread of Protestantism in Scotland offers him to make mischief.
sentences.zh: 所以，当他看到苏格兰新教的传播能为他制造麻烦时，他那双小小的、像猪一样的精明眼睛一下子亮了起来。

sentences.en: So, actually, four months after Mary was born, he'd written to the Earl of Arran, the slippery guy who's become the regent.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，在玛丽出生四个月后，他就写信给阿兰伯爵了，也就是那个成了摄政王的滑头家伙。

sentences.en: And he proposes a raft of Protestant-style reforMs.
sentences.zh: 并且他提出了大量新教风格的改革方案。

sentences.en: So, he says that the Scots should have the Bible freely available in their own language, that tracks opposed to the English Reformation should be cracked down on.
sentences.zh: 所以，他说苏格兰人应该能够在自己的语言中自由阅读圣经，并打击那些反对英国宗教改革的路线。

sentences.en: So, that's kind of pro-Catholic ones.
sentences.zh: 所以，这有点像亲天主教的立场。

sentences.en: And also, he tells the Earl of Arran, you know, get on and dissolve the monasteries.
sentences.zh: 而且，他还对阿兰伯爵说，你知道的，去把修道院解散了吧。

sentences.en: It's absolutely brilliant.
sentences.zh: 这简直太棒了。

sentences.en: And he very overtly frames this, not as being justified by, you know, the true religion of Protestantism or whatever, but to say, it's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 而且他非常公开地把这包装起来，不是用什么新教的真理来为之辩护，而是说，这太棒了。

sentences.en: You'll make so much money.
sentences.zh: 你们能赚好多钱。

sentences.en: Look how much cash I've got.
sentences.zh: 看看我赚了多少现金。

sentences.en: It's great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Tommy, you can fat shame Henry VIII as much as you like, but those are all actually quite good ideas.
sentences.zh: 汤米，你管亨利八世叫胖子怎么嘲讽都行，但这些其实都是相当不错的点子。

sentences.en: The Scots would have done well to profit from them.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰人本来完全可以从中受益的。

sentences.en: Anyway.
sentences.zh: 总之。

sentences.en: You're right, because the Earl of Arran, who is actually quite a devout Catholic, I mean, he's pretty tempted by this.
sentences.zh: 你说得对，因为实际上相当虔诚的天主教徒阿兰伯爵，我是说，他对此非常心动。

sentences.en: Henry, in his own way, is Catholic as well.
sentences.zh: 亨利以他自己的方式，其实也是个天主教徒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: There's a kind of streak of opportunism there that I think is as evident in the higher reaches of Scotland as in England.
sentences.zh: 这里有一种机会主义的倾向，我认为它在苏格兰的高层和在英国一样明显。

sentences.en: And there's a further aspect of Scottish affairs that Henry finds tempting, which is that having a girl as a queen means that she's obviously going to have to be married off.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰事务中还有另一个让亨利垂涎的方面，那就是有一个女作为女王意味着她显然得嫁出去。

sentences.en: And Henry's heir is a young boy, you know, the male heir that he'd done so much to try and secure.
sentences.zh: 而亨利的继承人是个小男孩，你知道的，他费尽心思想要确保的男性继承人。

sentences.en: And this boy, Edward, he's going to need a wife.
sentences.zh: 而这个男孩，爱德华，他需要一个妻子。

sentences.en: So Henry says to Arran, why don't we match them up?
sentences.zh: 所以亨利对阿兰说，我们把他们凑成一对怎么样？

sentences.en: It would be brilliant.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: And so in July 1543, Henry and the Earl of Arran duly sign a treaty in Greenwich, just down the Thames from London.
sentences.zh: 于是在1543年7月，亨利和阿兰伯爵在伦敦泰晤士河下游的格林威治正式签署了一项条约。

sentences.en: And its provisions from the point of view of Henry VIII are brilliant.
sentences.zh: 从亨利八世的角度来看，它的条款简直绝了。

sentences.en: So Mary is going to be brought up with English-speaking attendants, so not Scots-speaking attendants.
sentences.zh: 所以玛丽将由说英语的侍从抚养长大，而不是说苏格兰语的侍从。

sentences.en: She'll grow up, you know, with a nice received pronunciation accent.
sentences.zh: 她长大后，你知道的，会带着好听的标准发音口音。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Then at the age of 10, she'll marry Prince Edward.
sentences.zh: 然后在他10岁的时候，她将嫁给爱德华王子。

sentences.en: Their children will rule a united kingdom of Great Britain.
sentences.zh: 他们的后代将统治一个统一的大不列颠王国。

sentences.en: Arran will commit to pursuing essentially Protestant policies.
sentences.zh: 阿兰将致力于推行基本上是新教的政策。

sentences.en: So all of these are wins for Henry and England.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些对亨利和英国来说都是胜利。

sentences.en: The only concession that Henry grants to the Scots is that Mary's kingdom will continue to be called Scotland and retain its ancient laws and liberties.
sentences.zh: 亨利对苏格兰人做出的唯一让步是，玛丽的王国将继续被称为苏格兰，并保留其古老的法律和自由。

sentences.en: It'll be a bit of a dual monarchy, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想这有点像二元君主制。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's the plan.
sentences.zh: 对，这就是计划。

sentences.en: Like an Austro-Hungarian empire.
sentences.zh: 就像奥匈帝国一样。

sentences.en: So there's a massive road not taken.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一条没有选择的巨大分岔路。

sentences.en: What a historical what if that is?
sentences.zh: 这真是一个历史假设啊！

sentences.en: Because if that had happened, the story of the 17th century and thereafter would have been completely different.
sentences.zh: 因为如果那发生了，17世纪及以后的历史将完全不同。

sentences.en: And why does it not happen when they've done this deal in Greenwich?
sentences.zh: 既然他们在格林威治达成了这笔交易，为什么后来没有发生呢？

sentences.en: Because Arran finds it impossible to take the rest of the country with him.
sentences.zh: 因为阿兰发现根本无法让全国其他地方跟随他。

sentences.en: Most people in Scotland do not want to end up, as they would see it, subordinated to England, even the Protestants.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰的大多数人并不想最终落得他们所认为的臣服于英国的下场，哪怕是新教徒也是如此。

sentences.en: And at this point, most people in Scotland are still very much Catholic.
sentences.zh: 而在此时，苏格兰的大多数人仍然非常信奉天主教。

sentences.en: So it's just impossible.
sentences.zh: 所以这根本不可能。

sentences.en: But more than that, he has a very, very effective opponent in Scotland in the form of Mary of Guise, the French mother of Mary, Queen of Scots,
sentences.zh: 但不仅如此，他在苏格兰遇到了一个非常非常强劲的对手，那就是苏格兰女王玛丽的法籍母亲吉斯的玛丽，

sentences.en: who is absolutely determined not to let her daughter become a kind of an English queen.
sentences.zh: 她绝对坚决不让自己的女儿变成某种英国女王。

sentences.en: And so this is one of the reasons why she's removed Mary to Stirling Castle, which is effectively impregnable.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是她把玛丽转移到斯特灵城堡的原因之一，那座城堡可以说是坚不可摧。

sentences.en: It had been a personal gift from James V to Mary of Guise.
sentences.zh: 那是詹姆斯五世给吉斯的玛丽的私人礼物。

sentences.en: So it's her own personal stronghold.
sentences.zh: 所以那是她自己的私人据点。

sentences.en: This means that Arran cannot get his hands on the infant queen.
sentences.zh: 这意味着阿兰无法控制这个幼小的女王。

sentences.en: I mean, if he had been able to, then maybe history would have been different if Mary had been kind of packed off to London.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果他当时能控制的话，那如果玛丽被打包送到伦敦，历史也许就会不同了。

sentences.en: I mean, who knows what would have happened?
sentences.zh: 我是说，谁知道会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: But Mary of Guise has her daughter and Stirling is not going to be captured.
sentences.zh: 但吉斯的玛丽掌握着她的女儿，斯特灵城堡是不会被攻陷的。

sentences.en: More than that, of course, Mary of Guise is very effective at playing, you know, the rival would-be strongmen of Scotland.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，当然，吉斯的玛丽非常擅长玩弄苏格兰那些争权夺势的强人们。

sentences.en: So as well as Arran, there is Lennox.
sentences.zh: 所以除了阿兰，还有伦诺克斯。

sentences.en: She drops subtle hints to Lennox that perhaps, you know, she might be interested in marrying him.
sentences.zh: 她向伦诺克斯暗示，也许，你知道的，她可能有兴趣嫁给他。

sentences.en: You know, this would be great for Lennox.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这对伦诺克斯来说太棒了。

sentences.en: That might help solidify his claim to the throne.
sentences.zh: 这可能有助于巩固他对王位的声索。

sentences.en: And at the same time, Mary of Guise, very kind of cunning and clever.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，吉斯的玛丽非常狡猾和聪明。

sentences.en: However, she's also giving a kind of little hint of her ankle to another of Scotland's most powerful noblemen.
sentences.zh: 然而，她也向苏格兰另一位最有权势的贵族抛出了诱饵。

sentences.en: There's a guy called Patrick Hepburn, and he is the Earl of Bothwell.
sentences.zh: 有个家伙叫帕特里克·赫本，他是博思韦尔伯爵。

sentences.en: And he's a very big player.
sentences.zh: 而且他是个重量级人物。

sentences.en: So he, by hereditary right, is the Lord Admiral of Scotland, and he's the Sheriff of Edinburgh.
sentences.zh: 因此，根据世袭权利，他是苏格兰的海军上将，也是爱丁堡的治安官。

sentences.en: So to control both the fleet and the capital, I mean, that's quite something.
sentences.zh: 所以既能控制舰队又能控制首都，我的天，这可真了不起。

sentences.en: And his castle is, I mean, I think probably the most sinister, brooding and atmospheric castle in the whole of Britain.
sentences.zh: 而且他的城堡，我的天，我认为可能是整个不列颠最阴森、压抑且极具氛围感的城堡。

sentences.en: And it's called the Hermitage.
sentences.zh: 它叫寄宿所城堡。

sentences.en: It's right on the borders of England and Scotland.
sentences.zh: 它正好位于英格兰和苏格兰的边界上。

sentences.en: And it's in what at the time was the most dangerous area in the whole of Britain.
sentences.zh: 而且它位于当时整个不列颠最危险的地区。

sentences.en: It was called the Debatable Lands.
sentences.zh: 这里被称为争议之地。

sentences.en: It was kind of given over to bandits called Reavers.
sentences.zh: 这里基本上被被称为“劫掠者”的土匪所盘踞。

sentences.en: And I don't know if you've ever been to it, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我不知道你有没有去过那里。

sentences.en: It's like something out of Game of Thrones.
sentences.zh: 这就像《权力的游戏》里的场景。

sentences.en: We say that about so much that we talk about.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的好多地方都这么说。

sentences.en: But it really is, if you imagine the kind of terrifying place you would not want to end up, this is the castle, the Hermitage.
sentences.zh: 但它真的就是这样，如果你想象一下那种你绝不想落入的恐怖地方，就是这座城堡，寄宿所城堡。

sentences.en: And so unsurprisingly, with all these attributes, the Earl of Bothwell, he doesn't suffer from self-esteem issues.
sentences.zh: 所以毫不奇怪，凭借所有这些特质，博思韦尔伯爵一点也不缺乏自尊心。

sentences.en: So Henry VIII's ambassador to Scotland described him as the most vain and insolent man in the world, full of pride and folly.
sentences.zh: 因此，亨利八世驻苏格兰的大使形容他是世界上最虚荣、最无礼的人，充满傲慢与愚蠢。

sentences.en: Poor old Aaron.
sentences.zh: 可怜的阿兰。

sentences.en: He's up against Lennox.
sentences.zh: 他的对手有伦诺克斯。

sentences.en: He's up against the Earl of Bothwell.
sentences.zh: 他的对手有博思韦尔伯爵。

sentences.en: And he's up against Mary of Guise.
sentences.zh: 他的对手还有吉斯的玛丽。

sentences.en: And basically, he finds himself with no option but to reverse ferret.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他发现自己别无选择，只能一百八十度大转弯。

sentences.en: So, you know, he's very changeable.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，他非常反复无常。

sentences.en: Whatever he determineth today, he changes tomorrow, as Mary of Guise had said of him.
sentences.zh: 正如吉斯的玛丽对他的评价那样：他今天决定的事，明天就会改变。

sentences.en: And so, having signed this treaty with Henry VIII, he gets back to Scotland, discovers nobody's in favour of it.
sentences.zh: 因此，在与亨利八世签署了这份条约后，他回到苏格兰，发现根本没人支持它。

sentences.en: And so, he completely rips it up.
sentences.zh: 于是，他彻底把它撕毁了。

sentences.en: He abandons the English alliance.
sentences.zh: 他抛弃了与英国的联盟。

sentences.en: He stops pretending to be Protestant.
sentences.zh: 他不再假装自己是新教徒。

sentences.en: And he submits to attending Mary's coronation alongside Lennox and Mary of Guise.
sentences.zh: 并且他屈服了，同伦诺克斯和吉斯的玛丽一起出席了玛丽的加冕礼。

sentences.en: So, that's what he's doing, holding the crown over Mary.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是他正在做的事，把王冠举在玛丽头上。

sentences.en: And this is obviously very, very humiliating for him.
sentences.zh: 这显然对他来说非常非常羞辱。

sentences.en: But it's also humiliating for Henry VIII in England.
sentences.zh: 但这对于英格兰的亨利八世来说也是一种羞辱。

sentences.en: Right, and Henry VIII, so Mary of Guise is delighted.
sentences.zh: 没错，亨利八世——所以吉斯的玛丽欣喜若狂。

sentences.en: But Henry VIII is absolutely furious, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 但亨利八世绝对暴跳如雷，对吧？

sentences.en: And actually...
sentences.zh: 而且实际上……

sentences.en: Livid.
sentences.zh: 气急败坏。

sentences.en: Yeah, he demands vengeance.
sentences.zh: 对，他要求复仇。

sentences.en: So, what are we, 1544, April 1544?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们是在什么时候，1544年，1544年4月？

sentences.en: He tells one of the Seymours, so Jane Seymour's brother Edward.
sentences.zh: 他告诉了其中一个西摩，也就是简·西摩的弟弟爱德华。

sentences.en: And he basically says, get into Scotland.
sentences.zh: 他基本上说，杀进苏格兰去。

sentences.en: Put all to fire and sword, burn Edinburgh town.
sentences.zh: 用烈火和刀剑摧毁一切，把爱丁堡镇烧为平地。

sentences.en: So raised and defaced when you've sacked and gotten what you can of it, as there may remain forever a perpetual memory of the vengeance of God, for their falsehood and disloyalty.
sentences.zh: 当你们洗劫了它并能拿走的都拿走之后，将其夷为平地并毁坏面貌，以便永远作为上帝对他们虚伪和背叛的惩罚的永恒记忆。

sentences.en: Put all the men and women and children to the sword.
sentences.zh: 把所有的男人、女人和孩子统统处死。

sentences.en: Do all this, do all that.
sentences.zh: 把这都做了，把那都做了。

sentences.en: Destroy all the villages.
sentences.zh: 摧毁所有的村庄。

sentences.en: He's not messing around.
sentences.zh: 他可不是在开玩笑。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, Seymour leads a massive English army into Scotland.
sentences.zh: 于是，西摩率领一支庞大的英国军队进入了苏格兰。

sentences.en: And what follows is the most brutal war of destruction that the English have ever waged in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是英国人在苏格兰发动过的一场最为残酷的毁灭之战。

sentences.en: And obviously, there have been quite a few brutal wars of destruction.
sentences.zh: 显然，以前也有过不少残酷的毁灭之战。

sentences.en: And it goes on for eight years.
sentences.zh: 这场战争持续了八年。

sentences.en: It outlasts Henry VIII himself.
sentences.zh: 它甚至比亨利八世本人活得还久。

sentences.en: And it was memorably termed by Sir Walter Scott in the early 19th century as the rough wooing.
sentences.zh: 19世纪初，沃尔特·司各特爵士给它起了一个令人难忘的名字叫作“狂暴求婚”。

sentences.en: So, basically, there's this idea that you go and destroy everything in your path.
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上就是这样一种想法：你前去摧毁你路上的一切。

sentences.en: And this is somehow supposed to persuade the Scots to give Mary Queen of Scots to Prince Edward in London.
sentences.zh: 而这居然被认为能够说服苏格兰人把苏格兰女王玛丽交给伦敦的爱德华王子。

sentences.en: And so, on one level, this is obviously self-defeating because it only confirms the majority of Scots in their kind of ancestral loathing for the English.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，这显然是自取灭亡，因为它只会加深大多数苏格兰人对英国人祖传的厌恶。

sentences.en: And also, of course, playing into Mary of Guise's hands, really, it only confirms them in their view of France as their natural kind of essential ally.
sentences.zh: 而且当然，这也正中吉斯的玛丽下怀，这只会让他们更加确信法国才是他们天然的核心盟友。

sentences.en: But, having said that,
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，

sentences.en: I think the most striking thing about the rough wooing, this kind of brutal English campaign against the Scots,
sentences.zh: 我认为关于“狂暴求婚”，这场英国对苏格兰的残酷战役，最引人注目的地方,

sentences.en: isn't that it kind of gives fresh impetus to the kind of traditional Scottish anglophobia.
sentences.zh: 并不是它给传统的苏格兰反英情绪注入了新的活力。

sentences.en: But what's most amazing, what's most unexpected, is that actually not everyone in Scotland is alienated by it.
sentences.zh: 而是最令人惊奇、最出乎意料的是，实际上并非苏格兰的所有人都对此感到疏离。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that there's now a constituency of support for the English as co-religionists, as fellow Protestants,
sentences.zh: 原因在于，现在出现了一个支持英国的支持群体，他们将其视为同信仰者、同为新教徒，

sentences.en: that actually can survive all the kind of the bloodshed and the slaughter and the ruin and the burning that the English are now inflicting on Scotland.
sentences.zh: 这实际上能够在英国人现在带给苏格兰的所有流血、屠杀、废墟和烈火中存活下来。

sentences.en: That the Reformation has got a sufficient hold on Scottish opinion that ties of religion are coming to seem, to some Scots,
sentences.zh: 宗教改革在苏格兰的舆论中已经站稳了脚跟，以至于宗教纽带在一些苏格兰人看来，

sentences.en: more important than the traditional hatred of the English.
sentences.zh: 比传统的对英国人的仇恨更加重要。

sentences.en: But it's also, surely, that thing that always happens when you have a smaller country and a larger country.
sentences.zh: 但这也是理所当然的，每当一个小国和一个大国并存时，总会发生这种事。

sentences.en: There's always going to be a faction who see the opportunities and align themselves with the big, overbearing neighbour,
sentences.zh: 总会有一派人看到机会，与那个专横的大邻居结盟，

sentences.en: just because of the internal dynamics of kind of core politics.
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是因为核心政治的内部动态。

sentences.en: There's always ins and outs.
sentences.zh: 总有各种内幕和门道。

sentences.en: So if there are people who hate the English, there's always mileage to be had, surely, in allying yourself with a very powerful patron across the border.
sentences.zh: 所以如果有人讨厌英国人，那么与国境那头一个非常强大的靠山结盟，肯定总能捞到好处。

sentences.en: No?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, kind of, but essentially that would be seen by Scots in the centuries since the Wars of Independence as treason.
sentences.zh: 我是说，某种程度上是吧，但本质上，自独立战争以来的几个世纪里，苏格兰人会把这视为叛国。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: You know, you would be a traitor for doing that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你这么做就是个叛徒。

sentences.en: What has changed with the Reformation is that there are now Scots who can say, well, my conscience requires me to ally myself
sentences.zh: 宗教改革带来的改变是，现在有些苏格兰人可以说了，好吧，我的良知要求我与那些

sentences.en: with, you know, fellow people who have cast off the Whore of Babylon.
sentences.zh: 抛弃了“巴比伦大淫妇”的同道中人结盟。

sentences.en: And that, in turn, does enable a kind of novel political faction to develop, which sees an alliance with England as something that is preferable to the traditional French alliance,
sentences.zh: 而这反过来，确实使得一种新颖的政治派别得以发展，他们认为与英国结盟比传统的法兰西同盟更可取，

sentences.en: because the French alliance doesn't come without strings either.
sentences.zh: 因为法兰西同盟同样附带各种条件。

sentences.en: France is even more of a preponderant power than England.
sentences.zh: 法国甚至是一个比英国更具压倒性的力量。

sentences.en: And so it does mean that, to a degree, the Scots are subordinated.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实意味着，在某种程度上，苏格兰人受到了控制。

sentences.en: And so there is now scope for kind of pro-English and pro-French factions actually to be a kind of genuine dynamic in Scottish politics.
sentences.zh: 因此，现在亲英和亲法派系实际上成为苏格兰政治中一股真正动力的空间已经打开了。

sentences.en: And that, in turn, means, you know, if you are a player in Scottish politics, you can kind of switch between them.
sentences.zh: 这反过来又意味着，如果你是苏格兰政治的一个玩家，你可以在它们之间摇摆。

sentences.en: And I guess the classic example of this is Lennox.
sentences.zh: 我想这方面的经典例子就是伦诺克斯。

sentences.en: Mary of Guise has been kind of saying, maybe I'll marry you, whatever.
sentences.zh: 吉斯的玛丽之前一直说，也许我会嫁给你，管他的。

sentences.en: Maybe I will.
sentences.zh: 也许我会。

sentences.en: Maybe I won't.
sentences.zh: 也许我不会。

sentences.en: But she'd actually been playing him along.
sentences.zh: 但她其实一直在耍他。

sentences.en: She's been playing the field.
sentences.zh: 她一直在脚踩多条船。

sentences.en: She's been winking at the Earl of Bothwell as well.
sentences.zh: 她同时也对博思韦尔伯爵暗送秋波。

sentences.en: And so Lennox realizes this, realizes that Mary of Guise has no intention of marrying him and has a massive strop and openly turns pro-English.
sentences.zh: 所以伦诺克斯意识到了这一点，意识到吉斯的玛丽根本没有打算嫁给他，于是大发雷霆，公开转向亲英。

sentences.en: He basically yells at Mary of Guise, says, you're terrible.
sentences.zh: 他基本上对吉斯的玛丽大吼大叫，说，你太糟糕了。

sentences.en: You're an absolute slag.
sentences.zh: 你简直是个彻底的荡妇。

sentences.en: I'm off.
sentences.zh: 我不干了。

sentences.en: Storms off to England.
sentences.zh: 气冲冲地去了英格兰。

sentences.en: And when he's there, remember, he has a claim to the Scottish throne.
sentences.zh: 当他到那里时，记住，他对苏格兰王位拥有继承权。

sentences.en: He assigns this claim to the Scottish throne to the English king.
sentences.zh: 他将这项对苏格兰王位的继承权转让给了英格兰国王。

sentences.en: Oh, that's a big decision.
sentences.zh: 哦，那是一个重大的决定。

sentences.en: It is a big decision.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个重大的决定。

sentences.en: And he is very royally rewarded.
sentences.zh: 而且他得到了极其丰厚的皇家奖赏。

sentences.en: So he's given extensive lands in Yorkshire, in the north of England.
sentences.zh: 因此，他在英格兰北部的约克郡被授予了广袤的土地。

sentences.en: But he's also given the hand of one of Henry VIII's nieces in marriage.
sentences.zh: 但同时，他还迎娶了亨利八世的一位侄女。

sentences.en: And this is potentially, I mean, looking ahead, a very momentous development, because it means that any children, and perhaps more specifically, any sons he has,
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，这可能是一个极其重大的发展，因为这意味着他所生下的任何孩子，尤其是儿子，

sentences.en: will not just have Stuart blood in his veins, but the blood of the Tudors as well.
sentences.zh: 不仅血管里流淌着斯图尔特的血液，还将拥有都铎王朝的血统。

sentences.en: And so therefore, potentially, a claim to the throne of England as well as Scotland.
sentences.zh: 因此，潜在地，他也对英格兰和苏格兰的王位都拥有了继承权。

sentences.en: All of this, of course, well in the future.
sentences.zh: 当然，这一切都还在遥远的未来。

sentences.en: If you're Mary of Guise, presumably, you look at this and you think, oh, this is terrible.
sentences.zh: 如果你是吉斯的玛丽，你大概会看着这一切心想：天哪，这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: This is a very ominous development.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常不祥的发展。

sentences.en: Oh, does she not care?
sentences.zh: 哦，难道她不在乎吗？

sentences.en: She thinks it's fine.
sentences.zh: 她觉得这挺好的。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: I mean, she thinks Lennox is, I mean, kind of peripheral figure.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在她眼里，伦诺克斯只是个无足轻重的小人物。

sentences.en: Who cares?
sentences.zh: 谁在乎呢？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: She's got the rough wooing going on all around outside Stirling Castle.
sentences.zh: 当时斯特灵城堡周围到处都在进行“粗暴求婚”战争。

sentences.en: The castle is so secure that she can basically ride it out.
sentences.zh: 城堡是如此安全，以至于她基本上可以安然度过危机。

sentences.en: So she sits in Stirling Castle with her daughter, Mary Queen of Scots, even as the countryside is on fire.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管乡村正处于战火之中，她依然和女儿——苏格兰女王玛丽一起安坐在斯特灵城堡里。

sentences.en: And the brilliant thing from her point of view is that the blame for the rough wooing does not fall on her, but on Aaron, who completely gets the blame for it.
sentences.zh: 从她的角度来看，最妙的是，“粗暴求婚”的骂名并没有落到她头上，而是全背在了阿伦身上，他把罪责全揽了下来。

sentences.en: And she's able to take advantage of this to leverage her own position of authority within Scotland.
sentences.zh: 她得以利用这一点，来巩固自己在苏格兰的权力地位。

sentences.en: So Aaron is forced to accept her presence alongside him in the Privy Council and in Parliament.
sentences.zh: 因此，阿伦被迫接受她与自己一同在枢密院和议会中参政。

sentences.en: And this now means that Mary of Guise doesn't have to operate in the traditional way that women do in Scotland, kind of behind the scenes.
sentences.zh: 这意味着吉斯的玛丽不再需要像苏格兰女性传统那样在幕后行事。

sentences.en: She has her hands directly on the levers of power.
sentences.zh: 她直接将权力掌握在了自己手中。

sentences.en: And so she's therefore in pole position to push her dream policy, which is to marry her daughter directly into the French royal family.
sentences.zh: 因此，她处于最有利的位置来推行她梦寐以求的政策，那就是将女儿直接嫁入法国王室。

sentences.en: And this is obviously a great way of renewing the old alliance between Scotland and France and potentially subordinate Scotland permanently to French interests.
sentences.zh: 这显然是重修苏格兰与法国旧同盟的绝佳途径，并有可能使苏格兰永久沦为法国利益的附庸。

sentences.en: But more than that, I mean, you know, she's a Guise.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，你知道的，她可是吉斯家族的人。

sentences.en: She's part of this incredibly ambitious family in France.
sentences.zh: 她是法国那个野心勃勃的家族的一员。

sentences.en: To marry her daughter into the royal family of France, I mean, that's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 把女儿嫁进法国王室，这简直太棒了。

sentences.en: It would be to kill two birds with one stone.
sentences.zh: 这就是一石二鸟。

sentences.en: So, you know, she has everything to play for here.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，她有充分的资本去博取这一切。

sentences.en: And it works, right?
sentences.zh: 而且成功了，对吧？

sentences.en: Because in 1547, two things happen that play very much into her hands.
sentences.zh: 因为在1547年，发生了两件非常顺应她心意的事情。

sentences.en: And the first one is the death of the French king, François I, or Francis I.
sentences.zh: 第一件是法国国王弗朗索瓦一世的驾崩。

sentences.en: So he was the great guy, massive nose, always wrestling Henry VIII.
sentences.zh: 他是个了不起的人，长着个大鼻子，总是和亨利八世摔跤。

sentences.en: He was Henry VIII's big rival.
sentences.zh: 他是亨利八世的主要对手。

sentences.en: Hanging out with Leonardo da Vinci, all of that.
sentences.zh: 和达芬奇厮混在一起，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's dead.
sentences.zh: 他死了。

sentences.en: And now his son Henry, or Henry, becomes Henry II.
sentences.zh: 现在他的儿子亨利成为了亨利二世。

sentences.en: And Henry's big pals with the Guise family.
sentences.zh: 而亨利与吉斯家族是铁哥们。

sentences.en: His advisors are Guises, Tom.
sentences.zh: 他的谋士都是吉斯家族的人，汤姆。

sentences.en: Nice one.
sentences.zh: 不错嘛。

sentences.en: Her brothers, actually, Mary of Guise's brothers, François and Charles.
sentences.zh: 实际上是她的兄弟们，吉斯玛丽的兄弟，弗朗索瓦和查尔斯。

sentences.en: And because of that, basically, she has a massive in with the new king of France.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，她基本上和新任法国国王搭上了极其硬的关系。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So François and Charles, it's called Francis and Charles.
sentences.zh: 所以弗朗索瓦和查尔斯，英文里叫弗朗西斯和查尔斯。

sentences.en: We're very Anglophone.
sentences.zh: 我们真是太英式了。

sentences.en: So Francis is a military man.
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯是个军人。

sentences.en: He's going to become the Duke of Guise.
sentences.zh: 他将成为吉斯公爵。

sentences.en: He's the most brilliant military strategist in France.
sentences.zh: 他是法国最出色的军事战略家。

sentences.en: He's been playing a key part in France's wars in Italy that we talked about in the Medici episodes.
sentences.zh: 他在美第奇番外篇中提到过的法国意大利战争中发挥了关键作用。

sentences.en: And his brother, Charles, is the Cardinal of Lorraine.
sentences.zh: 他的弟弟查尔斯是洛林枢机主教。

sentences.en: And he's, you know, one of a long line of Machiavellian cardinals who are kind of brilliant behind the scenes operators, gifted ministers.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他是众多马基雅维利式枢机主教中的一员，是在幕后运筹帷幄、极有天赋的杰出大臣。

sentences.en: You know, so Richelieu and Mazarin, the next century, very much part of that tradition.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，后一个世纪的黎塞留和马扎然，很大程度上就属于这种传统。

sentences.en: And having these two guys, Francis and Charles, at the side of Henry II, Mary of Guise now has a hotline directly to the king.
sentences.zh: 有了弗朗西斯和查尔斯这两个人在亨利二世身边，吉斯玛丽现在可以直接与国王热线沟通了。

sentences.en: But actually, what ironically serves to make the match between the infant queen of Scots into the royal French line absolutely a banker is a disastrous Scottish military defeat.
sentences.zh: 但讽刺的是，真正让幼小的苏格兰女王与法国王室联姻十拿九稳的，是一场灾难性的苏格兰军事惨败。

sentences.en: The third of the three great military debacles that Scotland suffers in the 16th century.
sentences.zh: 这是苏格兰在16世纪遭遇的三大军事惨败中的第三次。

sentences.en: And the context for this is, again, the rough wooing.
sentences.zh: 而这一切的背景，依然是“粗暴求婚”。

sentences.en: So you mentioned Edward Seymour, the brother of Jane Seymour, so the uncle of Henry's son, Edward, who is now Edward VI, back in London.
sentences.zh: 所以你提到了爱德华·西摩，简·西摩的兄弟，也就是亨利现在身在伦敦的儿子、已成为爱德华六世的爱德华的舅舅。

sentences.en: He's the Lord Protector for Edward VI.
sentences.zh: 他是爱德华六世的护国公。

sentences.en: And in September 1547, he launches another massive invasion of Scotland.
sentences.zh: 1547年9月，他对苏格兰发动了又一次大规模入侵。

sentences.en: He advances on Edinburgh.
sentences.zh: 他向爱丁堡推进。

sentences.en: And the Earl of Arran has raised just about every man that he can to confront this onslaught.
sentences.zh: 阿伦伯爵几乎动员了他能集结的所有人来抵抗这场猛烈进攻。

sentences.en: And he masses his forces on the hills above a small hamlet called Pinky, which I think is a great name.
sentences.zh: 他将军队集结在平基这个名字很好听的小村庄上方的山丘上。

sentences.en: And this is probably the largest Scottish army ever assembled.
sentences.zh: 这可能是集结过的规模最大的苏格兰军队。

sentences.en: And an English observer seeing it is very intimidated.
sentences.zh: 一个看到这一幕的英格兰观察员感到非常震撼。

sentences.en: And he says that the spears of the Scots were as thick as the bristles of a hedgehog.
sentences.zh: 他说苏格兰人的长矛浓密得就像刺猬的刺一样。

sentences.en: And the result of this exceptional Scottish effort is utter defeat.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰人付出非凡努力的结果却是彻底的惨败。

sentences.en: Arran runs away.
sentences.zh: 阿伦逃跑了。

sentences.en: He flees scant with honour, as the description has it.
sentences.zh: 正如描述所说，他带着耻辱仓皇逃窜。

sentences.en: And behind him, he leaves 10,000 dead Scots on the battlefield.
sentences.zh: 在他身后，战场上留下了1万具苏格兰人的尸体。

sentences.en: And Mary of Guise is so panicked by the news of this debacle that for the first time, she worries that Stirling Castle will not be able to hold out.
sentences.zh: 吉斯的玛丽被这场惨败的消息吓坏了，她第一次担心斯特灵城堡将无法坚守。

sentences.en: And so she flees with her baby daughter westwards to a remote priory, the priory of Inchmahome, some 80 miles west of the battlefield of Pinky.
sentences.zh: 于是她带着年幼的女儿向西逃到一个偏远的修道院——英奇马霍姆修道院，距离平基战场以西约80英里。

sentences.en: And set on an island in a lock.
sentences.zh: 它坐落于湖中的一座小岛上。

sentences.en: And just to give a taster of what is to come, this is not the first island in a lock that Mary, Queen of Scots, will find herself on.
sentences.zh: 为了提前预览即将发生的事情，这并不是苏格兰女王玛丽将要呆过的唯一一座湖中孤岛。

sentences.en: How tantalising.
sentences.zh: 多么诱人啊。

sentences.en: Something to look forward to.
sentences.zh: 真让人期待。

sentences.en: What an exciting thought.
sentences.zh: 多么令人兴奋的想法。

sentences.en: So basically, because the Scots have had this massive debacle and they've shamed themselves on the battlefield, they now have to leap into bed with the French.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，因为苏格兰人经历了这场惨败，并在战场上蒙羞，他们现在不得不投向法国人的怀抱。

sentences.en: They don't want to be subordinate to England.
sentences.zh: 他们不想臣服于英格兰。

sentences.en: They have to be subordinate to anybody.
sentences.zh: 他们不得不臣服于某人。

sentences.en: They'd rather be with the French.
sentences.zh: 他们宁愿和法国人在一起。

sentences.en: And Henri, Henry II, the King of France, thinks, brilliant, this is my chance.
sentences.zh: 法国国王亨利二世心想，太棒了，这是我的机会。

sentences.en: I can now get in bed with the Scots and probably marry this girl.
sentences.zh: 我现在可以和苏格兰人结盟，并很可能娶这个女孩了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he acts very, very rapidly because the situation is actually quite dangerous.
sentences.zh: 他行动得非常非常迅速，因为局势实际上相当危险。

sentences.en: Because should the English get hold of Mary, Queen of Scots, it's game over for everybody.
sentences.zh: 如果英格兰人抓住了苏格兰女王玛丽，那对所有人来说就全完了。

sentences.en: So what Henry does is he sends a massive expeditionary force.
sentences.zh: 因此亨利采取的行动是派遣了一支庞大的远征军。

sentences.en: It lands in Leith, the port that serves Edinburgh in June 1458, 130 ships, kind of 5,500 infantry, 1,000 cavalry.
sentences.zh: 它于1458年（应为1548年）6月在利斯登陆，这是爱丁堡的港口，有130艘船，大约5500名步兵，1000名骑兵。

sentences.en: And they kind of basically roll the English back.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上把英格兰人逼退了。

sentences.en: The English are forced back towards Berwick.
sentences.zh: 英格兰人被迫退回伯威克。

sentences.en: The French have a meeting with the Earl of Arran at a nunnery in a small town called Haddington, which is about 20 miles east of Edinburgh.
sentences.zh: 法国人在距离爱丁堡以东约20英里的小镇哈丁顿的一座修女院与阿伦伯爵会面。

sentences.en: And here they sign a treaty.
sentences.zh: 在这里他们签署了一项条约。

sentences.en: And it's agreed that the Earl of Arran will become a Duke of France.
sentences.zh: 双方商定阿伦伯爵将成为法国公爵。

sentences.en: So he becomes the Duke of Châtel-Hérault.
sentences.zh: 因此他成为了沙特尔罗公爵。

sentences.en: And it is also agreed, more significantly, that Mary, Queen of Scots, who at this point is still only five and a half, will marry the eldest son of Henry II, the Dauphin Francis.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，双方还商定，当时年仅五岁半的苏格兰女王玛丽将嫁给亨利二世的长子——法国王太子弗朗西斯。

sentences.en: And so as a result of this, the Queen of Scots is destined to become the Queen as well of France.
sentences.zh: 因此，作为结果，苏格兰女王注定也将成为法国王后。

sentences.en: And she is shipped off to France very, very rapidly.
sentences.zh: 她非常非常迅速地被送往了法国。

sentences.en: So the next month, the 29th of July, she boards the ship that will take her to France.
sentences.zh: 所以在下一个月，即7月29日，她登上了将带她去法国的船。

sentences.en: She leaves the great fortress of Dumbarton on the Clyde.
sentences.zh: 她离开了克莱德河畔伟大的敦巴顿堡垒。

sentences.en: And the ship she boards is the Royal Galley, the galley of the King of France himself, that the King has sent to Scotland, this particular mark of honour to Mary.
sentences.zh: 她登上的船是皇家大帆船，也就是法国国王本人的御用大帆船，是国王特意派往苏格兰以向玛丽致以这种特殊荣誉的船只。

sentences.en: And her escort is the fleet that had sailed to Leith and has now sailed around the northern coast of Scotland, back down to the Clyde.
sentences.zh: 她的护航舰队正是之前航行到利斯、现在绕过苏格兰北部海岸、返回克莱德河的舰队。

sentences.en: And all the French crews are very impressed by the Queen of Scots.
sentences.zh: 所有的法国船员都对苏格兰女王印象深刻。

sentences.en: They find her very pretty, very charming, very poised.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得她非常漂亮、非常迷人、非常有风度。

sentences.en: You know, she's an adorable little Muppet, basically.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她基本上就是一个极其可爱的洋娃娃。

sentences.en: I mean, how poised can you be at five years old?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，五岁时你能有多有风度？

sentences.en: Very, apparently.
sentences.zh: 显然，非常非常有。

sentences.en: I'm very sceptical of this, Tom.
sentences.zh: 对此我深表怀疑，汤姆。

sentences.en: I think five-year-olds, by and large, are not poised.
sentences.zh: 我认为五岁的孩子大体上是没有什么风度的。

sentences.en: She is simultaneously poised and charming.
sentences.zh: 她既有风度又迷人。

sentences.en: And there's these aspects of her character that will run throughout her life.
sentences.zh: 她的性格中确实有这些特质，并将贯穿她的一生。

sentences.en: I know you love Mary Queen of Scots.
sentences.zh: 我知道你很爱苏格兰女王玛丽。

sentences.en: I absolutely do believe it.
sentences.zh: 我绝对相信这一点。

sentences.en: You've drunk the iron brew, I think it's fair to say, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我觉得可以说你已经中了苏格兰的毒了。

sentences.en: Well, we will see.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们拭目以待。

sentences.en: But just to say, they're actually held up for a week because there are storMs.
sentences.zh: 但不得不说，他们实际上被耽搁了一周，因为遇到了风暴。

sentences.en: I mean, storms in the Scottish summer, who's heard the like?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，苏格兰夏天的风暴，谁听说过这种事？

sentences.en: But very impressively, again, Dominic, Mary doesn't fall seasick.
sentences.zh: 但非常令人佩服的是，多米尼克，玛丽并没有晕船。

sentences.en: Oh, amazing.
sentences.zh: 哦，太惊人了。

sentences.en: How remarkable that all these French sailors used to life at sea do fall seasick, but this five-year-old girl doesn't.
sentences.zh: 多么了不起，所有这些习惯了海上生活的法国水手都晕船了，而这个五岁的小女孩却没有。

sentences.en: I absolutely believe you.
sentences.zh: 我绝对相信你。

sentences.en: It's not the French sailors, it's her retainers.
sentences.zh: 不是法国水手，是她的随从们。

sentences.en: And we know that because they wrote about it later in life.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以知道这一点，是因为他们后来在生活中写到过。

sentences.en: Anyway, so eventually they sail off and they're rounding Cornwall again.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，最终他们扬帆起航，再次绕过康沃尔。

sentences.en: There's a massive storm.
sentences.zh: 遭遇了一场巨大的风暴。

sentences.en: The rudder of the galley gets smashed.
sentences.zh: 大帆船的舵被撞碎了。

sentences.en: She single-handedly sails the ship to France.
sentences.zh: 她单枪匹马把船开到了法国。

sentences.en: And no, again, poise, I think is the word.
sentences.zh: 不，再说一次，我觉得“有风度”这个词很贴切。

sentences.en: Not a sign of fear.
sentences.zh: 没有一丝恐惧的迹象。

sentences.en: Perfectly calm.
sentences.zh: 极其镇定。

sentences.en: Incredibly admirable.
sentences.zh: 令人难以置信地钦佩。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, you've got a report here.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，你这里有一份报告。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So they finally land.
sentences.zh: 所以他们终于登陆了。

sentences.en: They make land on French soil on the 13th of August, 1548.
sentences.zh: 他们于1548年8月13日踏上了法国的土地。

sentences.en: And Dominic, you've been sceptical, but do you want to know what one of the commanders of the French fleet said about her?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你一直对此持怀疑态度，但你想知道法国舰队的一位指挥官是怎么评价她的吗？

sentences.en: No, I don't.
sentences.zh: 不，我不想。

sentences.en: But you're going to read it anyway.
sentences.zh: 但你无论如何都要读出来。

sentences.en: I absolutely am, because I think the listeners want to know.
sentences.zh: 我绝对要读，因为我认为听众们想知道。

sentences.en: So this French commander said, she, Mary, is one of the most perfect creatures that ever was seen.
sentences.zh: 所以这位法国指挥官说，她，玛丽，是有史以来最完美的生物之一。

sentences.en: Such a one as from this very young age, with its wondrous and estimable beginnings, has raised
sentences.zh: 从如此年轻的时候起，就以其奇妙而令人尊崇的开端，引发了

sentences.en: such expectations that it is not possible to hope for more from a princess on this earth.
sentences.zh: 如此高的期望，以至于不可能对地球上的任何一位公主抱有更多的希望。

sentences.en: So I don't think you can argue with that.
sentences.zh: 所以我想你对此无可反驳。

sentences.en: Well, Elizabeth I will have something to say about that, Tom.
sentences.zh: 好吧，伊丽莎白一世对此会有一番说辞的，汤姆。

sentences.en: And if listeners want to find out how Mary measures up to these gushing previews, how she gets on in France, why she ends up going back to Scotland, and all of the extraordinary
sentences.zh: 如果听众想知道玛丽如何经受住这些天花乱坠的预告的考验，她在法国过得怎么样，她为什么最终决定返回苏格兰，以及她余生中所有非凡、

sentences.en: melodramatic details of the rest of her life, the explosions, murders, all kinds of plots and conspiracies, just an amazing, amazing story.
sentences.zh: 戏剧性的细节，那些爆炸、谋杀、各种阴谋诡计，这绝对是一个极其精彩的故事。

sentences.en: So the next episode is coming in a couple of days, but you can get all five remaining episodes
sentences.zh: 所以下一集将在几天后推出，但你可以通过在 therestishistory.com 注册加入 The Rest is History Club

sentences.en: of this epic series by signing up to The Rest is History Club at therestishistory.com.
sentences.zh: 来获取这部宏大系列的其余全部五集。

sentences.en: And on that Scottish bombshell, goodbye.
sentences.zh: 带着这个苏格兰重磅炸弹般的爆料，我们再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
